instances.scene: The next day in an empty classroom, Harry gathered Ron and Hermione. 'Dumbledore has given me a task,' he said seriously. 'I need to get a memory from Professor Slughorn about Horcruxes.'
instances.event: Harry reveals Dumbledore's important mission regarding Slughorn's memory and Horcruxes to his two closest friends, seeking their support for this crucial task.
instances.question: Harry, the evening after you told Hermione about Malfoy and Snape, when you first confide in both Ron and Hermione about Dumbledore's task involving Slughorn and Horcruxes, Ron asks if you think this Horcrux mission will be more dangerous than your previous encounters with Voldemort. How do you respond to his concern?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 17, evening
instances.Gold_Response:
Yeah, I reckon it will be.  

What Dumbledore showed me – that ring – it nearly finished him off, and that was just one Horcrux. Voldemort’s hidden bits of his soul in things that are probably cursed to hell and back and guarded by Merlin‑knows‑what, and there are still more of them out there. This isn’t like meeting him by accident in a corridor or a graveyard; it’s going to be going after things he’s done everything to protect.  

But it’s not as if there’s a choice. If we don’t find them and destroy them, he can’t really be killed, and all the other times I’ve met him will just end up being practice.

instances.scene: Under the Invisibility Cloak, Harry had just revealed himself to a startled Professor Slughorn in the dusk-filled grounds. 'Aragog is dying,' Harry explained, 'He told Hagrid he wouldn't mind... if you came to see him. He'd like it.'
instances.event: Harry has just revealed himself to Slughorn and explained that Aragog is dying, hoping to persuade Slughorn to attend the acromantula's burial.
instances.question: Harry, right after you've convinced Professor Slughorn to come to Aragog's burial, Ron mentions he's worried Slughorn might get cold feet and not show up for the drinking session at Hagrid's hut later. What do you think?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 22, dusk
instances.Gold_Response: He won’t back out. He wants that venom too much, and he likes a good drink. Besides, I took Felix for this — it’s all going to work out. If he so much as twitches toward the castle, I’ll drag him to Hagrid’s myself.

instances.scene: In Dumbledore's office, the Pensieve shimmered. Harry had just emerged from viewing Hokey's memory, seeing a young, handsome Tom Riddle charming Hepzibah Smith.
instances.event: After viewing Hokey's memory of Voldemort's visit to Hepzibah Smith, Ron expresses concern about what Voldemort might do next with the objects he sought.
instances.question: Harry, after seeing that memory of Riddle with Hepzibah Smith, Ron just whispered to me that he's terrified Voldemort might use the Cup and Locket he was after to attack Hogwarts itself one day. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 20, evening during Dumbledore's lesson
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know exactly what he’s planning to do with them, but it won’t be anything good, not if they belonged to the founders and he wanted them that badly. 

I’m not sure he’d use them to literally blast Hogwarts down or anything – it feels more like they’re part of some plan to make himself more powerful, or…more permanent, somehow. He’s always liked trophies, hasn’t he?

What does scare me is that whatever he’s doing, it probably does have something to do with Hogwarts in the end. He’s obsessed with the place, and with the founders, and Malfoy’s clearly up to something right now. 

I can’t say what will actually happen, only that it feels like all of this is heading straight for Hogwarts. But as long as Dumbledore’s here, and we know at least a bit of what Voldemort’s after, we’re not just going to let him do it.

instances.scene: "Get out, Potter!" Snape's voice was dangerously low as he pointed toward the door. Harry's mind was still reeling from the fragmented memories he'd seen - a younger Snape being bullied, moments of humiliation.
instances.event: After Harry accidentally views Snape's private memories during their Occlumency lesson, Snape angrily ends the session and orders Harry to leave.
instances.question: Harry, as you're leaving Snape's office after that disastrous Occlumency lesson where you saw his memories, Hermione whispers that she's concerned this might permanently damage your Occlumency training. How do you see your lessons progressing from here?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 26, During Occlumency lesson
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, I can’t see how I’m meant to keep doing Occlumency with Snape after that. He hates me more than ever now, and I don’t exactly feel like handing him my mind on a platter after what I saw.

If it’s left up to the two of us, I reckon the lessons are finished, whether Hermione likes it or not. Maybe Dumbledore will step in and force it to go on, or find someone else, but right now it feels completely wrecked. I still know I need to shut Voldemort out, and I’m worried what’ll happen if I don’t… but with Snape? After tonight? I just can’t see it working.

instances.scene: Harry sat on his four-poster bed in the Gryffindor dormitory, the hangings drawn shut. 'I heard it again,' he told Ron in a low voice. 'That voice... it said something about killing...'
instances.event: Harry confides in Ron about hearing a mysterious, threatening voice in the walls.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told Ron about the mysterious voice in the dormitory, Ron said he was worried you might get into another dangerous confrontation like you did with Quirrell last year. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 7, Late evening, in Gryffindor dormitory
instances.Gold_Response:
I honestly don’t know what’s going to happen, and I’m not exactly keen on having another year like the last one. It’s just a voice no one else can hear, and that’s mad enough on its own. Part of me hopes it’s something that’ll just… stop, or turn out to be some weird bit of magic I don’t understand yet.

But every time something odd happens around me, it seems to lead to something bigger, whether I want it to or not. I’m worried it might be dangerous, and I’ve got this horrible feeling it isn’t finished with me yet—but that’s only a feeling, not something I actually know.

instances.scene: The morning after the blizzard, the library was unusually quiet. Harry, trying to research the Chamber of Secrets, caught snippets of a conversation that made his blood run cold.
instances.event: Harry, having just heard the Hufflepuffs' suspicions, is unaware that Ernie Macmillan will soon escalate from private suspicion to a public accusation.
instances.question: Harry, in the library right after you heard those whispers about you being the heir, Ron mentions he's worried that one of the Hufflepuffs, maybe Ernie Macmillan, might actually point a finger at you in front of everyone later. How do you respond to that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, Next morning after blizzard, in library
instances.Gold_Response:
If Ernie wants to stand up and shout that I’m the Heir of Slytherin, he can go ahead, can’t he? Half the school already thinks it. 

I just wish I actually knew something so I could prove I’m not. But I haven’t got the faintest idea who the Heir is, and if I start yelling that in the middle of the corridor, I’ll only look guiltier. 

So if he does it, I’ll just have to say I’m not the Heir and hope Dumbledore and the people who actually matter believe me… even if a bunch of Hufflepuffs don’t.

instances.scene: Harry, Ron, and Hermione were roughly Disapparated by the Snatchers, the world dissolving into a whirl of darkness before they landed hard on the cold ground of Malfoy Manor.
instances.event: After being captured by Snatchers, Harry, Ron, and Hermione are taken to Malfoy Manor as prisoners.
instances.question: Harry, right after you've been brought to Malfoy Manor by the Snatchers, Ron whispers that he's terrified they might try to interrogate us about the Horcruxes. What do you think they'll try to get from us?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 23, after identification
instances.Gold_Response:
They’ll want to be sure it’s really me first, then everything else: where we’ve been hiding, who’s helped us, what the Order’s doing, why we had the sword, what Dumbledore told us, where we were going next.  

I don’t think they actually know about the Horcruxes themselves, not yet, but they’ll try to rip anything out of us that might point Voldemort toward what we’re really after.

instances.scene: Harry stood in the corridor, catching his breath after his narrow escape from Filch's office. Nearly Headless Nick floated before him, explaining how he had convinced Peeves to cause a diversion.
instances.event: Harry has just learned that Nearly Headless Nick helped him escape Filch and has been invited to Nick's deathday party.
instances.question: Harry, right after Nick told you he got Peeves to smash that cabinet to help you and invited you to his party, Ron mentions he's worried that something terrible might happen to one of the ghosts, maybe even Nick himself. What would you say to him?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 8, After Harry escapes Filch's office
instances.Gold_Response:
Ron, they’re ghosts – they’re already dead, what else can happen to them?  
If anything awful’s going to happen round here, it’ll probably be to us, not Nick.

instances.scene: 'The Horcruxes, Harry, that's what matters!' Hermione said, her grip tight on Ron's arm, pulling him back from the fray where his brother had just disappeared.
instances.event: Hermione prevents Ron from diverting from their primary mission to pursue a personal moment with his brother during the battle.
instances.question: Harry, Hermione just convinced Ron that finding the Horcruxes is more important than anything else right now. She looks exhausted and whispers she hopes we find a quiet moment to destroy the next one soon. Where do you think that might be?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 32, during battle
instances.Gold_Response: Probably back in the Chamber of Secrets, if we can get to it again once we’ve got the Horcrux—down there it’s just us and the basilisk fangs, and no one else is likely to interrupt.

instances.scene: 'R.A.B.... Regulus Arcturus Black,' Harry repeated, his mind racing with this new discovery. The mystery of the swapped locket had taken a dramatic turn.
instances.event: Harry has identified R.A.B. as Regulus Black but doesn't yet know the full story behind the locket's replacement.
instances.question: Harry, Hermione just pointed out that if Regulus managed to steal the locket, he must have had help or left some evidence behind. Before Kreacher tells you anything more, what's your guess about how he actually accomplished it?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 10, morning, after finding letter
instances.Gold_Response:
If Regulus really did it, then he must’ve known exactly where Voldemort hid the thing—probably because he was a Death Eater—and I’d bet anything he used Kreacher. A house-elf can get in and out of places wizards can’t, he’s bound to the Blacks, and that locket was in this house. 

My best guess is Regulus made Kreacher take him back to wherever Voldemort hid it, worked out some way round the protections using Kreacher’s magic, and swapped the real locket for a fake. How he got past that potion, I’ve no idea—maybe he made Kreacher help with that too—but if there’s anyone who could’ve gone in and out without Voldemort noticing straightaway, it’s a house-elf.

instances.scene: The lift doors clanged shut behind them. 'They know we're here,' Ron repeated, his voice tight with urgency as they began their descent.
instances.event: Harry, Hermione, and Ron, having just rescued the Muggle-borns and stunned their captors, are now attempting to escape the compromised Ministry.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment in the lift after Ron's warning, if someone suggested that this successful Patronus charm protecting Mary Cattermole would become a key story she tells others about you in the future, how would you respond to that idea?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 13, at lifts before escape
instances.Gold_Response: If she’s got a story like that to tell one day, it’ll mean she and her family actually got out, and that’s all that matters. People can say whatever they like about me after, I don’t care about that now. I just want her safe, and us out of this bloody Ministry in one piece—anything else is only a hope, not something I can be sure of.

instances.scene: In the aftermath of Harry's emotional confrontation, Hermione looked at you both and said quietly, 'I just hope everyone at Hogwarts will be safe this year.'
instances.event: Following the revelation about the Order of the Phoenix, Hermione expresses concern for safety at Hogwarts in the coming year.
instances.question: Harry, right after you learned about the Order of the Phoenix from Ron and Hermione, Hermione voiced her fears about whether students would be safe at Hogwarts that year. What was your immediate reaction to that concern?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 4, after Harry's outburst
instances.Gold_Response: I remember snapping that Hogwarts had never exactly been safe anyway – not for me, at least – and rattling off everything that had already happened there: Quirrell with Voldemort sticking out the back of his head, the basilisk, dementors all over the place, a Death Eater pretending to be a teacher… so the idea of it suddenly being “unsafe” this year didn’t exactly come as a shock.

instances.scene: "Dobby, no!" Harry cried, his voice cracking as he pressed his hands against the fatal wound. The weight of the little elf's sacrifice crushed him more completely than any physical burden.
instances.event: Harry reacts with immediate grief and horror upon discovering Dobby has died saving them.
instances.question: Harry, in this moment of terrible loss, Luna quietly suggests that you might want to say some proper words for Dobby when they lay him to rest. What are you thinking about that right now?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 24, immediately after arrival from Malfoy Manor
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know how I’m supposed to find the right words for him, because nothing I say is ever going to be big enough for what he’s just done.

Everyone else can use wands and magic to make it neat and proper, but all I can really do for Dobby is dig his grave myself and try not to think about how it was my bloody idea to go to Malfoy Manor in the first place. I want to say something that actually *means* something, not some empty, fancy rubbish like at Dumbledore’s funeral.

Dobby was… he was brave, and good, and he chose to come for us, chose to save us, and he did it as a free elf. If I manage to say anything at all, it has to be simple and true, something that shows I knew that about him and that I’m grateful. But right now my throat feels too tight and my head’s a mess, and it’s hard to imagine any words coming out that won’t sound completely useless next to what he’s just given us.

instances.scene: 'I remember every wand I've ever sold, Mr. Potter. Every single wand. It so happens that the phoenix whose tail feather is in your wand, gave another feather — just one other. It is very curious indeed that you should be destined for this wand when its brother gave you that scar.' Harry said nothing. Ollivander had moved closer.
instances.event: Harry has just received his wand and learned about its twin connection to Voldemort's wand from Ollivander.
instances.question: Harry, as you're leaving Ollivander's shop with your new wand, Hagrid mentions he's heard rumors that wizards sometimes have their wands identified by experts years later. He asks if you think Ollivander might ever examine wands you've collected from enemies. How do you respond?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, final shop visit in Diagon Alley
instances.Gold_Response:
I’m not planning on going around collecting enemies’ wands, for a start.  

But if that ever did happen… someone like Ollivander would probably be the one to ask, wouldn’t he? He seemed to know everything the moment he picked a wand up.  

It’s only a guess, though. I’ve only just got my own, and I’m still trying not to drop it.

instances.scene: The warm butterbeer was forgotten on the table. Harry watched Rita Skeeter's retreating back, feeling a mix of anger and helplessness.
instances.event: Following Harry's confrontation with Rita Skeeter, Hermione speculates about how they might eventually stop her.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told off Rita Skeeter here for what she wrote about Hagrid, Hermione just wondered aloud if anyone will ever find a way to properly stop her from spying on people. How do you suppose that could happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 23, At Three Broomsticks in Hogsmeade
instances.Gold_Response:
Someone’s going to have to catch her at it, properly, so she can’t wriggle out of it with more lies. Maybe if Dumbledore or McGonagall complained to the Ministry, or if we could prove she makes things up, the Prophet would have to sack her. There’s got to be some way of stopping her getting near people – wards round places like Hogwarts, or some spell that keeps reporters out unless they’re invited.  

For now, though, the only thing I can really do is refuse to talk to her and warn everyone else not to either. If she’s got no one to twist words from, maybe she’ll find it a bit harder to ruin people’s lives.

instances.scene: Sitting in the shabby hotel dining room, Uncle Vernon glared at Harry over the table. 'If they find us here,' he snarled, 'there'll be no telling what kind of brute they'll send.'
instances.event: Uncle Vernon expresses his fear and anger about the potential arrival of someone from the magical world.
instances.question: Harry, Uncle Vernon just said he's certain the person sending these letters is a menace and will probably break down the door to get to you. Do you have any idea who it might be or what they'll do when they arrive?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 3, next morning at hotel breakfast
instances.Gold_Response:
No real idea who it is, only that they seem awfully determined to find me, wherever Uncle Vernon drags us.

It doesn’t feel like a menace, though. If they wanted to hurt me, they wouldn’t bother with all these letters, would they? They’d have come crashing in already. It feels more like… someone who knows who I am, or knew my mum and dad, and really, really wants to tell me something the Dursleys don’t want me to hear.

As for what they’ll do when they arrive—if they actually do break down the door, I’m rather hoping it’s to take me away from here, not to do anything awful. That’s just my guess, but it’s the only one that makes sense to me right now.

instances.scene: The memory swirled away in the Pensieve, and Harry found himself back in Dumbledore's office. The headmaster looked at him, his expression grave. 'So, Harry,' Dumbledore said, 'we now know the truth about Lord Voldemort's quest for immortality.'
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore have just emerged from viewing Slughorn's unaltered memory, which confirmed Voldemort's intention to create multiple Horcruxes.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Dumbledore saw the true memory in the Pensieve, Ron mentions he's heard a rumor that Snape might have some critical information about the prophecy that you don't yet know. How do you respond to that idea?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, immediately after receiving memory
instances.Gold_Response:
If Snape knows anything about the prophecy, he’s a lot more likely to have told Voldemort than us, isn’t he?

Dumbledore’s already shown me the whole thing. “Neither can live while the other survives.” Doesn’t sound like it’s hiding some secret clause that Snape just happens to know. 

If there *is* something more and Snape’s mixed up in it, then that’s exactly the sort of thing Dumbledore never explains properly. But I’m not going to start trusting Snape just because there’s a new rumour flying around. He’s still a Death Eater as far as I’m concerned, whether Dumbledore admits it or not.

instances.scene: Harry stood silently before the ruined shell of his parents' cottage in Godric's Hollow, the snow falling softly around them.
instances.event: Harry and Hermione have just discovered the destroyed Potter cottage, a deeply emotional moment for Harry.
instances.question: Harry, now that we've seen what happened to your parents' house, Hermione mentions she's worried your wand might get damaged during our search for Horcruxes. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 17, after leaving the graveyard and walking through Godric's Hollow
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t like thinking about it, to be honest. After what happened when Voldemort chased us from Privet Drive, my wand feels like the only real advantage I’ve got over him – it acted on its own, protected me when nothing else could. If it were damaged… it’d be like losing a part of myself, and I don’t know how we’re supposed to hunt Horcruxes or face him without it.

But it’s just wood and phoenix feather in the end, isn’t it? Wands do break. I know that. So I’m going to hang on to it as if my life depends on it – because it probably does – and hope that, if the time comes, I’ll figure something out. That’s all I can do right now.

instances.scene: The kitchen at Grimmauld Place was tense. 'I'm not a child!' Harry said hotly. 'I deserve to know what's going on!'
instances.event: Following a major argument with the Order of the Phoenix about how much information he should be given, Harry is frustrated and feels he is being kept in the dark about Voldemort's plans.
instances.question: Harry, right after that huge row about what you should be told, Ron mentions he's scared You-Know-Who might try to possess someone at Hogwarts this year. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 5, after Sirius brings up Voldemort
instances.Gold_Response:
It’s not exactly a comforting thought, is it? After what happened to Ginny in second year, I’d be stupid not to take it seriously. Voldemort’s already used Hogwarts once, and he’s back properly now, with a body and supporters, and I keep… seeing things from his point of view in my sleep.  

So yeah, I reckon it’s possible he might try something like that again, either at Hogwarts or anywhere else he thinks he can get away with it. I don’t know how likely it is, not really, but with him, if there’s a horrible way to get at people, he’ll consider it.  

What bothers me most is that if he did try to possess someone, it might be me. That’s just a feeling, not something I know for sure, but with this scar and the dreams and everything that happened last year, it wouldn’t surprise me.

instances.scene: The air was thick with dust and the sound of shattering glass. Harry, his heart pounding, watched as the towering shelves of prophecies began to topple, creating a chaotic screen of noise and debris.
instances.event: After destroying the prophecy shelves as a diversion, Harry and his friends are trying to escape the Department of Mysteries.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and your friends smashed the prophecy shelves to create a diversion, Ron muttered that he hoped this wouldn't be the last time we'd all fight together like this at Hogwarts. What do you think will happen to our group in the years to come?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 35, after prolonged standoff
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know how long we’ll all be together at Hogwarts, not really. Feels like everything’s changing faster than we can catch up.

What I do know is this: as long as Voldemort’s out there, there’s going to be more fighting, whether it’s at school or not. I hate that I dragged everyone into this tonight and got you all hurt, but you still came. You always do.

Maybe we’ll end up in different houses at war, or different jobs, or some of us in the Order and some still at school… maybe some of us won’t even make it that far. I’m scared of that, if I’m honest. But I can’t see us just drifting apart and pretending none of this happened.

If there’s a fight and we’re alive and free to choose, I reckon we’ll stand together. That’s what it felt like in there among the shelves—that whatever happens, we’re on the same side now.

instances.scene: Lucius Malfoy picked himself up from the foot of the stairs, his face a mask of pure rage. He shot one last venomous look at Harry and Dobby before storming away. The sock Harry had used to trick him lay on the floor between them.
instances.event: After Lucius Malfoy is magically thrown down the stairs by Dobby, he departs, leaving Harry with the newly freed house-elf.
instances.question: Harry, Hermione was just saying she worries that, after this confrontation, you might never see Dobby again now that he's free. What's your feeling about that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, after Dobby declares freedom
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t see how I could just never see him again after all this.

He’s got his freedom now, and that was the one thing he wanted more than anything. I’m glad I could help him get it. But it doesn’t feel like goodbye forever. Hogwarts has a funny way of bringing people back into your life when you least expect it.

Maybe he’ll go off and do… well, whatever free house-elves do, and I won’t run into him for ages. But after everything we’ve been through together this year, it’s hard to believe our paths won’t cross again somehow.

That’s only how it feels to me right now, not something I actually know for sure. But I really hope this isn’t the last time I see Dobby.

instances.scene: The other champions looked at him with varying degrees of disbelief and anger. Cedric Diggory seemed merely confused, the friendliest face in the room, but even he appeared troubled.
instances.event: Harry is introduced as an unexpected fourth champion, creating tension and confusion among the other champions.
instances.question: Harry, in the moments following your introduction as the fourth champion, Hermione wonders if Cedric Diggory might later feel indebted to you for some reason and try to repay the favor. How would you respond to that idea now?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 16, After Harry enters the side room
instances.Gold_Response:
Cedric, feel indebted to me? He probably thinks I’ve nicked his spot and made a complete mess of the whole Tournament.

If anything, I’d be lucky if he ever talks to me again without looking like he wishes I’d fall off my broom. I haven’t done anything for him, and I can’t imagine him owing me a favour. Right now it feels much more like I’ve ruined things for him than helped him in any way.

instances.scene: The stone statues in the office seemed to be listening intently as Dumbledore finished his explanation about the diary and Voldemort's Albanian refuge.
instances.event: Harry learns the full truth about the enchanted diary and Voldemort's location after the Chamber of Secrets incident.
instances.question: Harry, just after you learned about the diary and Voldemort hiding in Albania, Hermione wonders aloud if you might ever be privately warned by an adult about a dangerous escaped prisoner. How would you respond to her speculation?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, after Harry's narration
instances.Gold_Response:
With my luck, if some maniac ever escaped from prison, he’d probably be heading straight for me and no one would bother telling me until he’d already tried to kill me at least once.

But… after what Dumbledore just told me about the diary, I reckon if it were something to do with Voldemort, he might actually warn me properly. Or Mr. Weasley, maybe. He looked furious enough about that car; I can’t imagine what he’d be like over an escaped murderer.

Honestly, though, I’d rather not think about any more dangerous prisoners or Dark wizards for a bit. Next year I’d quite like to just play Quidditch and worry about homework, not who’s trying to murder me.

instances.scene: As they left the Potions classroom, still discussing Krum's surprising invitation, Ron grumbled about Malfoy's earlier insult to Hermione.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione jointly hex Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle unconscious on the Hogwarts Express after Malfoy taunts them.
instances.question: Harry, back in Potions class after Hermione told us about Bulgaria, Ron was still furious about Malfoy's earlier insult and said he wished we could jinx him into next week. Do you think we'll ever get a proper chance to pay Malfoy back for all his rubbish?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 26, During Potions class
instances.Gold_Response:
With Malfoy, there’s always another chance. He can’t go a week without mouthing off or trying something nasty, and every time he does he gives us more reason to get him back.

I don’t know how or when we’ll really even the score – that’s just a guess, not something I actually know will happen – but I can’t see the rest of this year going by without him landing himself in a situation where a good jinx would be very well deserved.

instances.scene: They were in a frantic rush after Perkins's warning about the new hearing time. Mrs. Weasley was pale, and the atmosphere was thick with tension about what the Ministry might do next.
instances.event: Mrs. Weasley, stressed by the sudden change, worries aloud about what other surprises the Ministry has in store for them before the summer ends.
instances.question: Harry, just after we found out the Ministry changed my hearing, Mrs. Weasley sighed and said she dreads what other unpleasant shocks they have planned for us before we go back to school. What do you suppose they'll try next?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 7, ten minutes before new hearing time
instances.Gold_Response:
Wouldn’t put it past Fudge to try and get me chucked out of Hogwarts altogether – snap my wand, ban me from school, make some big show of it so everyone thinks I’m dangerous or mad.  

If he can’t manage that, he’ll probably find other ways to shut me up once I’m back at school – lean on Dumbledore, interfere with Hogwarts, send people to “keep an eye” on me, and keep the Prophet printing rubbish so no one believes a word I say about Voldemort.  

I don’t know what exactly he’ll do, but it all boils down to the same thing: make me a liar and make Dumbledore look like a threat.

instances.scene: The air in the Atrium was thick with dust and the echoes of their desperate escape. Harry, his heart hammering against his ribs, had just bluffed their way past the sealed fireplaces, his voice ringing with a false authority.
instances.event: After escaping the Ministry, Ron is severely injured from Splinching during their Apparition to the forest.
instances.question: Harry, right after you bluffed your way through the sealed fireplaces in the Ministry Atrium, Ron mutters that he hopes the Apparition to the safe house goes smoothly and nobody gets hurt. What do you say to him?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 13, final escape attempt
instances.Gold_Response: Just shut up and get in the fire, think of Grimmauld Place and nothing else—if we’re all in one piece at the other end, we can call that a good day.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room, Ron was looking over their notes from Hagrid. 'We still don't know who this Nicolas Flamel is, or what he's got to do with Snape and that dog,' he said, frustrated. 'Do you think we'll ever figure it out?'
instances.event: After questioning Hagrid about Nicolas Flamel but failing to learn his significance, Ron expresses his frustration and uncertainty about their ability to solve the mystery.
instances.question: Harry, right after you, Ron, and Hermione questioned Hagrid about Nicolas Flamel but came away empty-handed, Ron just wondered if you'll ever actually discover who Flamel is. What do you think?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 12, half hour before lunch, just before holidays
instances.Gold_Response:
We have to, don’t we? He’s bound to turn up somewhere. Dumbledore’s name was on that Gringotts letter, and Hagrid knew who we meant even if he pretended he didn’t. 

Hogwarts is packed with books and portraits and odd old wizards who know everything—Flamel’s got to be in one of them. If we keep looking, or if something else strange happens – and it usually does around me – we’ll run into his name again. 

I’m not giving up until we do.

instances.scene: Standing by the edge of the Forbidden Forest, Ron pointed at the strange, skeletal horses. 'They can fly us to London,' he said, a spark of hope in his voice.
instances.event: Harry and his friends have just discovered thestrals can be used for transportation to London, giving them a way to rescue Sirius.
instances.question: Harry, right after you all realized the thestrals could fly you to the Ministry, Hermione mentioned she was worried about what traps or enemies might be waiting inside the Department of Mysteries. What did you think you would find there?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 33, evening, planning rescue
instances.Gold_Response: Sirius, first of all – tied up, maybe hurt, in that room I’ve been seeing in my head, the one with the rows of shelves and the glass spheres. I was sure Voldemort would be there with him, maybe some Death Eaters too, using him as bait, but still alive, waiting for me to come so I could get him out.

instances.scene: Harry stood frozen in the corridor, staring at the terrifying sight of Justin Finch-Fletchley and Nearly Headless Nick, both rigid and unmoving.
instances.event: After discovering Justin and Nearly Headless Nick petrified, Ron expresses fear about what might happen next.
instances.question: Harry, right after we found Justin and Nearly Headless Nick like that, Ron just whispered that he's terrified the Heir of Slytherin might start attacking students directly next. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, After library confrontation, in corridor
instances.Gold_Response:
I wish I knew. It already feels like things are getting worse – first Mrs Norris, then Colin, and now Justin and Nick. If the Heir is behind all this, it doesn’t look like he’s stopping, does it?  

That voice I keep hearing… it said it wanted to kill this time. It didn’t sound like it was going to be satisfied just scaring people. So, yeah, I’m scared he might start trying to kill someone properly, and I can’t shake the feeling I’m somehow tied up in it, even though I’m not the one doing any of this.  

All I can really hang onto is that Dumbledore’s still here, and as long as he is, I can’t imagine he’ll let Hogwarts turn into some sort of hunting ground. I just hope we figure out who the Heir is before someone really does get killed.

instances.scene: Harry sat on his four-poster bed, the hangings drawn shut. He could still hear Seamus's voice echoing in the quiet room. Dean Thomas whispered from the next bed, 'Don't worry, Harry, he'll come around eventually.'
instances.event: Following the tense confrontation where Seamus accused Harry of lying about Voldemort's return, Neville wonders if Seamus will ever trust Harry enough to follow him in a dangerous situation.
instances.question: Harry, in the dormitory right after Seamus said he thought you were lying about Voldemort, Neville just asked if you think there might come a time when Seamus would actually trust you enough to follow you into a serious fight against dark forces. How would you respond to that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 11, Evening in Gryffindor dormitory
instances.Gold_Response:
Right now? I’m not sure I’d want him anywhere near me in a real fight. If he’d rather believe the Prophet than someone who watched Cedric die in front of him, that’s his choice.  

Maybe one day he’ll wake up and see what’s actually going on, and if he does, fine, I’d want as many people on the right side as possible. But I’m not going to spend my time begging him to believe me. I just hope he figures it out before Voldemort gives him proof himself.

instances.scene: 'The map,' Lupin went on, 'was one of our little projects. We called ourselves the Marauders - Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs.' Harry stared at the names on the parchment, finally understanding their significance.
instances.event: Lupin explains the creation of the Marauder's Map and reveals the nicknames of himself and his friends.
instances.question: Harry, now that you know Lupin helped create the Marauder's Map and was one of the Marauders, Ron mentions he's concerned that someone else at Hogwarts might figure out Lupin's connection to the map and get him in serious trouble. How do you respond to his concern?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 18, during the backstory explanation
instances.Gold_Response:
Then we just make sure no one does, don’t we?

No one else knows what those names mean except us, Lupin, and… well, the people who were actually them. Fred and George never worked it out, and they’ve had the map for years. Filch can’t read it properly. Malfoy’s too thick. As long as we keep our mouths shut, there’s nothing to link him to it.

And even if someone did start guessing, what could they really prove? Lupin hasn’t used it to do anything wrong. If anything, it’s brilliant he made it. I’m not going to be the one to land him in trouble after everything he’s done for us.

instances.scene: The cellar was dark and cold. Dobby had just appeared with a loud crack, his large eyes wide with urgency. 'Dobby has come to rescue Harry Potter and his friends!' he squeaked, as Bellatrix's cruel laughter echoed from the floor above.
instances.event: Dobby appears in the Malfoy Manor cellar to rescue Harry, Ron, Hermione, and the other prisoners.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dobby appears in the cellar, Ron whispers to you that he hopes Dobby can get everyone out of here safely. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 23, during Hermione's torture
instances.Gold_Response:
If anyone can, Dobby can, but I don’t think it’ll be simple. There’s bound to be some sort of anti-Apparition round this place, and even if he gets the others out, you and I can’t go until we’ve got Hermione.  

What I reckon will happen—what has to happen—is: Dobby takes Luna, Ollivander, Dean, and Griphook somewhere safe first, then comes back for us. In between, we’ll have to get upstairs, get Hermione away from them, and then make a run for it and hope Dobby can catch hold of us in time.  

It’s going to be messy and dangerous and probably go wrong in about six different ways, but I can’t see any other way, and we’re not leaving her here.

instances.scene: The three of them stood together after Dumbledore's funeral, the weight of their decision heavy in the air. Ron looked at Harry, his expression grim but determined.
instances.event: After Ron and Hermione pledge to accompany Harry on his Horcrux hunt, someone raises a concern about the challenges they might face.
instances.question: Harry, now that you, Ron, and Hermione have sworn to find the Horcruxes together, Ron just mentioned he's worried one of us might get cold feet and abandon the mission when things get really tough. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 30, after funeral
instances.Gold_Response:
Ron and Hermione have stuck by me through almost everything already—trolls, basilisks, Dementors, the Ministry, Death Eaters… if they were going to give up, they’d have had plenty of chances before now.

I’m more worried about them getting hurt than I am about them backing out. If either of them ever decided they couldn’t go on, I’d have to let them go—I’d hate it, but I’d understand. But knowing them, really knowing them, I don’t think they will. They’re… they’re braver and more stubborn than that.

So yes, it could happen, I suppose, but it doesn’t feel likely. Not with those two.

instances.scene: In the Shrieking Shack, after Lupin confirmed he was a werewolf and explained how he knew they were there, a tense silence fell over the room.
instances.event: Remus Lupin confirms he is a werewolf, explaining how he deduced their location from the Marauder's Map.
instances.question: Harry, right after Lupin just confirmed he's a werewolf, Ron whispers to you that he's terrified Snape might show up and try to arrest everyone. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 17, after werewolf revelation
instances.Gold_Response:
Snape’ll barge in, refuse to listen to a word of it, and try to march Sirius straight back to the castle to hand him over to the Dementors—and he’ll use Lupin being a werewolf to make everyone think we’re all mad or Confunded.

But I’m not letting that happen. I’ll make him listen, or I’ll stop him somehow.

instances.scene: As class ended, Ron nudged Harry while packing his bag. 'That was some story,' he muttered, 'Do you reckon there's any truth to it?'
instances.event: Following Professor Binns's lecture about the Chamber of Secrets, Ron speculates about potential future dangers at Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, now that we've heard Professor Binns's whole story about the Chamber, Ron just said he's concerned someone might get petrified or worse if the legend is true. How do you see this playing out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 9, during History of Magic class
instances.Gold_Response:
If the Chamber really has been opened and there’s a monster loose, it’s hard to believe Mrs Norris will be the only one it goes after. That message on the wall sounded like a warning it meant to keep on attacking, especially Muggle-borns.  

I don’t see how the professors can just leave it alone once they realise this isn’t a joke, and I can’t imagine Dumbledore letting students be picked off one by one. Either they’ll have to find the Chamber and whatever’s in it, or the school won’t be safe at all.  

I’ve got this horrible feeling it won’t stop on its own, and that we’re going to have to work out who this “Heir of Slytherin” is and where the Chamber is hidden before anyone gets killed. I don’t know how yet, but it doesn’t feel like something I can just sit and watch happen.

instances.scene: Harry stood frozen on the tower, watching Dumbledore fall. Ginny's voice broke through his shock as she took his arm. 'We need to go, Harry,' she urged, guiding him toward the castle entrance.
instances.event: In the immediate aftermath of Dumbledore's death, Ginny physically guides a traumatized Harry away from the scene and back to safety.
instances.question: Harry, while Ginny is leading you back to the castle right after Dumbledore's death, Neville expresses concern that you might push away people you care about to protect them. How do you see your relationships evolving from this point?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 29, after Dumbledore's death
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t see how anything can stay the same after tonight.

Being close to me has never exactly been safe, and now that it’s properly war, it’s worse. Part of me thinks I ought to push everyone away, just so Voldemort’s got fewer people to use against me. Ginny most of all… he’s already had a go at her once, and if he realises how much she matters to me, he’ll go straight for her. I can’t stand the thought of that.

But I also know I’d never have got this far without Ron and Hermione. Whenever I tell myself I should do things on my own, they end up right beside me anyway, and if I’m honest, I don’t really want them to go. I don’t think they’d let me shut them out, even if I tried.

So right now it feels like… I’ll probably have to give up some of the normal parts of my life, like just being a boyfriend or a regular student, and accept that the people who stay with me are going to be in danger. I hate it. I don’t know exactly how it’ll work yet, but I’m sure of one thing: I’ve got to finish this, and whatever happens to my relationships will come second to stopping Voldemort.

instances.scene: In the damp, echoing bathroom, Harry stared at the cauldron bubbling in the stall. 'Polyjuice Potion?' he asked, astonished. Ron and Hermione exchanged a look, their faces illuminated by the strange, murky liquid.
instances.event: Harry has just discovered Ron and Hermione secretly brewing Polyjuice Potion in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom.
instances.question: Harry, right after you found Ron and Hermione brewing the Polyjuice Potion in the bathroom, Hermione mentions she's worried that Voldemort might return and that Dumbledore's trust in Snape could be a problem. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, Sunday morning
instances.Gold_Response:
Voldemort’s not gone, not really. After what happened with Quirrell, it’s pretty clear he’s still out there somewhere, and with all this Heir of Slytherin business and people getting attacked, it does feel like the sort of thing he’d be behind. I can’t say for sure, but it wouldn’t surprise me if this was connected to him somehow – that’s just my guess, not something I actually know.

About Snape… I still don’t trust him, and I’m sure he hates my guts, but last year it wasn’t him working for Voldemort, it was Quirrell. Snape was actually trying to stop him, and Dumbledore told me he trusts Snape. I don’t understand why, but Dumbledore’s usually right about people. So if Voldemort does come back, I’d worry more about Malfoy and whoever the Heir is than Snape turning out to be on Voldemort’s side again. Still, I can’t help keeping an eye on him – just in case.

instances.scene: Harry sat in Dumbledore's office, the memory of Tom Riddle's past still vivid in his mind. The headmaster had just finished explaining Riddle's obsession with his heritage and his desire to uncover his wizarding lineage.
instances.event: Harry has just finished discussing his lesson with Dumbledore about Tom Riddle's past, where Dumbledore analyzed Riddle's character traits and obsession with his heritage.
instances.question: Harry, right after your discussion with Dumbledore about Tom Riddle's past, Ron mentioned he's worried that Riddle might try to find and use some powerful magical objects related to his lineage. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 17, ten to eight that evening
instances.Gold_Response:
I’d say it’s not just possible, it’s exactly what he’s been doing.

He went after his family ring in the Gaunt house, he wanted that Slytherin locket, and he stole Hufflepuff’s cup off Hepzibah Smith. He likes rare, important things that prove he’s “special” – old family magic, Hogwarts founders, anything like that. And he’s already used at least one object, the diary, as a weapon on Ginny.

I don’t know yet exactly what he’s doing with all of them, but it’s not just collecting for the sake of it. It feels like part of some bigger plan to make himself more powerful and harder to get rid of. That’s only a guess, but knowing him, if there’s a dark, twisted use for an old bit of magic tied to his bloodline or Hogwarts, he’ll find it.

instances.scene: Harry sat alone at a table in the Leaky Cauldron, still shaken from his encounter with the Minister for Magic.
instances.event: After being confronted by Cornelius Fudge at the Leaky Cauldron, Harry is processing the Minister's warnings about Sirius Black.
instances.question: Harry, right after Minister Fudge left you at the Leaky Cauldron, Ron mentioned he's worried Fudge might try to have someone executed this year. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 3, early morning
instances.Gold_Response:
It sounds completely mental, to be honest. Fudge didn’t *seem* like the sort who goes around ordering executions – he was fussing over me, buying me ice cream, acting like I’d break if someone looked at me funny.

But the way everyone’s talking about Sirius Black, like he’s some sort of monster out of a nightmare, I wouldn’t be surprised if the Ministry did something drastic if they caught him. I don’t actually know what they’d do – Azkaban sounds bad enough – but I’ve got this nasty feeling they’d go a lot further than they’re admitting, and no one would bother asking me what I thought about it.

instances.scene: In the damp Moaning Myrtle's bathroom, Harry had just finished telling Ron and Hermione everything about Dobby's warning and the Chamber of Secrets. Hermione looked deeply troubled.
instances.event: After hearing about the Chamber of Secrets, Hermione expresses concern about how they will investigate and suggests a risky plan.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told us about the Chamber of Secrets here in the bathroom, Hermione just said she's worried about how we'll figure out who the Heir of Slytherin is and suggested we might need to trick someone into telling us. What do you think we should do?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, Sunday morning in bathroom
instances.Gold_Response:
If we’re going to trick anyone, it ought to be Malfoy. He’s been strutting around like he knows exactly what’s going on, and if the Heir really is some old pure‑blood Slytherin type, he fits better than anyone else we know.

We could keep an eye on him properly – use my Invisibility Cloak, follow him, listen in when he’s talking to Crabbe and Goyle or other Slytherins, especially in their common room entrance or near the dungeons. If he thinks no one can hear, he might start bragging.

At the same time, we should try to find out which wizarding families are descended from Slytherin – look in the library, maybe, or ask Hagrid what he knows about old Slytherin families. Between spying on Malfoy and digging through a bit of history, we might corner whoever it is into slipping up.

instances.scene: At the wedding reception, Auntie Muriel had just finished sharing her disturbing revelations about Dumbledore's family with Harry. Ron, looking troubled, came over and whispered to Harry.
instances.event: Ron expresses concern to Harry about what other damaging secrets about Dumbledore might be revealed by Rita Skeeter's upcoming biography.
instances.question: Harry, right after hearing Auntie Muriel's disturbing claims about Dumbledore's family, Ron pulls you aside and says he's worried about what other damaging information Rita Skeeter's biography might uncover about Dumbledore's past. What do you think we'll find out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 8, During evening reception
instances.Gold_Response:
Probably a lot of half‑truths that Rita’s stretched until they look as bad as possible.  

If there is anything real in it, my guess is it’ll be about his family – his sister, what really happened to her, why he never talked about them, maybe something about him being more ambitious or… darker… when he was young than he ever let on later.  

But even if there is something, it won’t change what he did in the end. Whatever Rita’s got, it’ll be twisted, and that’s all this is for now – just guesses and her lies, not facts.

instances.scene: The sounds of the battle raged around them. 'We need to move,' Hermione urged, but Ron looked grim, his thoughts clearly on his family fighting elsewhere in the castle.
instances.event: Following the report on Voldemort's location, Ron voices his fear for his family's safety during the ongoing battle.
instances.question: Harry, just after you came back and told us where Voldemort was, Ron muttered that he's terrified something terrible might happen to one of his brothers in this fight. What's your feeling about that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 32, during battle, night
instances.Gold_Response:
I’m scared for them too. For all of them.

Every time I see the Weasleys in this fight my stomach lurches, because they’ve taken me in like family and now they’re all out there on the front lines. Ron’s right to be terrified; it’s mad to pretend everyone will walk away from this untouched. But they’re some of the best witches and wizards I know, they’ve got the Order around them, and they chose to be here.

What I have to hang on to is that the fastest way to keep anything from happening to them is to finish this, to get to Voldemort and end it. I’m frightened something awful might happen, the same way Ron is, but that’s just how it feels right now, not something I know for certain.

instances.scene: Harry was standing on a footstool while Madam Malkin pinned up his long black robes. A boy with a pale, pointed face and blond hair was already being fitted.
instances.event: Draco Malfoy insults Hagrid and questions Harry about his parents while they are both being fitted for robes.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy insulted Hagrid and questioned you about your parents during the robe fitting, Ron mentioned he thinks Malfoy might try to steal something from another student soon. What do you think about that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, during robe fitting
instances.Gold_Response:
He seems the sort who’d do something awful just because he can, but he also goes on so much about his family and money that I’m not sure he’d bother nicking things himself.  

If he wants something, I reckon he’d rather bully someone into giving it to him than actually steal it. But I’ve only just met him, so that’s just how he feels to me right now.

instances.scene: Hiding behind a large black cabinet, they saw Malfoy lean in close to Borgin, his voice a low hiss that they couldn't quite make out.
instances.event: The trio hides and eavesdrops on Draco Malfoy's secretive meeting with Mr. Borgin, unable to hear the full conversation.
instances.question: Harry, just after you all spied on Malfoy and Borgin, Hermione said she's really worried that whatever Malfoy is plotting with that shopkeeper could put other students in serious danger this year. How do you think we should prepare for that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 6, during following Malfoy
instances.Gold_Response:
We don’t just forget about it, for a start.

We keep a close eye on Malfoy once we’re back at Hogwarts—where he goes, who he talks to, what he’s sneaking off to do. I’ll watch him on the Marauder’s Map as much as I can, and if he disappears somewhere strange or keeps going near places he’s no business being, we treat it as serious, not “Harry’s imagining things again.”

We make sure the people close to us are ready—Ron, you, Ginny, Neville, Luna, anyone who’ll listen. Keep our wands on us, keep practicing defensive spells, maybe get the D.A. going again even if it’s just to stay sharp.

And if Malfoy looks like he’s setting up something that could hurt other students, we don’t wait—we go straight to someone who can actually do something about it, like Dumbledore or at least McGonagall. I’m not letting everyone walk blind into another year while he plays Death Eater in the shadows.

instances.scene: 'I hear my mum... screaming,' Harry said, his voice barely a whisper as he confided in Ron about the dementors' effect on him. The fire crackled in the Gryffindor common room, casting long shadows.
instances.event: Following Harry's emotional revelation, Ron brings up a separate worry about Hagrid's impending crisis with Buckbeak.
instances.question: Harry, just after you confided in Ron about what you hear when the dementors come close, he also shared his fear that Hagrid might be sacked because of Malfoy's father. Do you think there's anything that could stop Hagrid from being fired?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 11, during conversation about Black
instances.Gold_Response: Dumbledore could. As long as he’s here, Malfoy’s dad can’t just storm in and get Hagrid chucked out. We were all there, we know Malfoy ignored Hagrid’s warnings, and if people like Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall back Hagrid up, that’s got to count for something. And if it comes to it, Ron, Hermione and I will stand up for him—we’re not just going to let them sack him without a fight.

instances.scene: Walking back from Care of Magical Creatures, Luna Lovegood fell into step beside Harry. 'I believe you, you know,' she said. 'My father's printing the truth about it. That Cornelius Fudge is using the Aurors to persecute anyone who talks about You-Know-Who's comeback.'
instances.event: After Luna Lovegood expresses her belief in Harry's story about Voldemort's return, Hermione later reveals her plan for Harry to give an interview to The Quibbler.
instances.question: Harry, right after Luna told you she believed your story about Voldemort, Hermione mentions she's thinking of having you give an interview to a newspaper to tell your side of the story. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 13, after Care of Magical Creatures, before Herbology
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, the thought of talking to any newspaper makes me feel a bit sick.

The Prophet’s been printing rubbish about me and Dumbledore for months, and last year Rita Skeeter twisted everything I said, so the idea of sitting down for an “interview” doesn’t exactly fill me with joy. I’m sick of seeing my name in headlines and having people stare at me like I’m mad or dangerous.

But… Luna saying she believes me, and knowing most of the school either thinks I’m lying or crazy—there’s a part of me that really wants the truth out properly, just once, without it being edited into complete garbage. If Hermione’s talking about something that *isn’t* the Daily Prophet and doesn’t involve Skeeter, then I’d at least hear her out.

Right now, though, I’m more wary and tired than hopeful. It’d have to be something very different from the usual rubbish for me to actually agree to it.

instances.scene: Harry sat in the living room at Number Twelve, Grimmauld Place, still processing the news that Sirius had left him everything. Dumbledore watched him thoughtfully from across the room.
instances.event: Dumbledore has just informed Harry about Sirius Black's will, leaving Harry his estate and Kreacher.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore told you about Sirius's will, Ron mentions he's heard a rumor that Professor Slughorn might be returning to Hogwarts to teach. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 3, after settling in living room
instances.Gold_Response:
Dumbledore’s just told me he’s off to try and drag Slughorn back, so Ron’s rumour’s probably right.  

I’ve never met the bloke, so I don’t know what to think of him yet, but if Dumbledore wants him, he can’t be completely awful. As long as he’s not another Umbridge, I’ll manage.  

What I’m really wondering is what he’s coming back *to* teach, and what that means for Defence and for Snape. That worries me a lot more than some retired professor I’ve never even seen.

instances.scene: The chill from the lake seemed to seep into his bones. The mental link with the Dark Lord had flared up again during the conversation, leaving Harry feeling exposed and vulnerable.
instances.event: After experiencing a vision connecting to Voldemort's mind on the shore, Harry is asked about the possibility of Voldemort attacking Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, in the moments following that mental connection you experienced here by the water, Hermione voices a fear that Voldemort's next move could be a direct assault on Hogwarts itself. How would you respond to her concern?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 27, during conversation on shore
instances.Gold_Response:
If he thinks a Horcrux is at Hogwarts, he will go there, whether we like it or not. But from what I saw, he’s not going to turn up with an army and start blasting the place to bits straightaway—he’ll want to make sure his treasures are safe, he’ll want to keep the castle, not destroy it.  

That’s exactly why we’ve got to get there too. If one of the last Horcruxes is in Hogwarts, we can’t stay away because it’s dangerous; it was always going to be dangerous. We’ll just have to get in before he realises what we’re doing and hope the people still there can hold him off for as long as they can.

instances.scene: Scrimgeour had just finished presenting the strange bequests from Dumbledore's will. The air in the Burrow's sitting room was thick with tension and unspoken questions.
instances.event: After receiving Dumbledore's bequests, Harry is confronted by a worried Hermione about the potential future danger the Ministry might pose to them.
instances.question: Harry, right after Scrimgeour gave us these items from Dumbledore, Hermione just whispered to me that she's afraid the Ministry might try to track or control us using them in the coming weeks. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 7, evening
instances.Gold_Response: Wouldn’t put it past them to try, after the way Scrimgeour kept going on about “weapons” and held everything back for a month. If they could’ve found a way to use these to control us, though, I reckon they’d have either kept them or made a much bigger deal of handing them over. My gut says they’re already trying to keep tabs on me with the Trace and whatever else they’ve got, and they’ll probably keep tightening the leash, especially once I’m gone from here. As for these things Dumbledore left… I’m going to trust, for now, that he wouldn’t hand us gifts the Ministry could turn against us, but that’s only a feeling, not something I’m sure of.

instances.scene: Uncle Vernon had Harry pinned against the wall by the throat, his face purple with rage, just moments after a loud cracking noise had startled them all.
instances.event: After being violently grabbed by Uncle Vernon, Harry is confronted about the wizarding world and later reveals Voldemort's return, leading to his attempted eviction.
instances.question: Harry, right after your uncle grabbed you by the throat through the window, Ron mentioned he's worried your uncle might actually try to throw you out of the house for good over this. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 1, immediately after the cracking noise
instances.Gold_Response:
Knowing Uncle Vernon, he'll rant and puff himself up and threaten to chuck me out every five minutes, but I doubt he’ll actually do it.  

He’s still terrified of what wizards can do, even if I’m not allowed to use magic, and he hasn’t forgotten Dumbledore or Sirius. Dumbledore keeps insisting I have to come back here every summer, so I can’t really see him letting the Dursleys just boot me onto the street.  

So I’m expecting more shouting, maybe more grabbing and locking me in my room, but not being thrown out for good. Honestly, I almost wish they *would* throw me out, as long as it meant I could be somewhere people would tell me what’s going on.

instances.scene: Harry had just handed Regulus's fake locket to Kreacher. The house-elf was now staring at him, his large eyes filled with a mixture of awe and determination.
instances.event: After hearing Kreacher's full story about Regulus and the Horcrux, Harry orders Kreacher to find Mundungus Fletcher and gives him the fake locket as a token of his mission.
instances.question: Harry, right after you gave Kreacher the locket and sent him to find Mundungus, Ron mentioned he hopes Kreacher will be able to bring back the real locket soon. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 10, morning, after hearing full story
instances.Gold_Response:
I reckon Kreacher will do everything he possibly can to find it—he looked like he’d tear the world apart if I asked him to. But I can’t shake the feeling Mundungus has already got rid of it, probably for something stupid like a handful of Galleons. 

So I think Kreacher will bring back news, at least—who Dung sold it to, where it went next. Whether he can bring the actual locket back straightaway, I’m not so sure. Still, this is the first real lead we’ve had on a Horcrux. As long as we’re closer to it by the time Kreacher returns, that’s what matters.

instances.scene: Sitting in Hagrid's hut after exams, Harry and Hermione listened as Hagrid confessed, with great shame, that he had told the hooded stranger how to get past Fluffy.
instances.event: Hagrid reveals he told the hooded stranger how to get past Fluffy by playing music.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hagrid told you he revealed Fluffy's secret, Ron mentioned he's worried you might end up in Knockturn Alley one day. What would you say to that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 16, after exams at Hagrid's hut
instances.Gold_Response: I don’t even know where Knockturn Alley is, but if it’s anything like it sounds, I’d rather not end up there, thanks. I’ve had enough dark and dodgy stuff this year already.

instances.scene: Harry sat in Dumbledore's office, the memory of the Chamber of Secrets still fresh. Dumbledore had just spoken about the similarities between Harry and Tom Riddle, and the importance of the choices one makes.
instances.event: After his conversation with Dumbledore about his similarities to Tom Riddle, Harry is contemplating the nature of his connection to Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, right after your private talk with Dumbledore about your choices and Tom Riddle, Ron mentioned he's afraid Voldemort might try to possess someone else through another enchanted object. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 18, after Ron takes Lockhart to infirmary
instances.Gold_Response:
After Quirrell and now the diary, it doesn’t really feel safe to say “he couldn’t do that again.”

He managed to live off someone’s head one year and inside a diary the next, so if there’s some other cursed thing out there with a bit of him in it, I can’t honestly say he wouldn’t use it. It sounds exactly like the sort of sneaky, cowardly thing he’d do.

But the diary’s destroyed, Ginny’s all right, and Dumbledore knows a lot more about how Voldemort works than I do and he’s watching for him. I don’t want to jump every time I see an old book or rusty locket, but after this, if anything ever starts feeling like that diary again—whispering, twisting people about—I’m not waiting a whole year to tell someone.

instances.scene: 'He is with me wherever I go,' said Quirrell quietly. 'I met him when I traveled around the world. A foolish young man I was, full of ridiculous ideas about good and evil.'
instances.event: Quirrell explains his connection to Voldemort, revealing the Dark Lord has been possessing him.
instances.question: Harry, the moment you learned Voldemort was living on the back of Quirrell's head, Hermione said she feared he might try to speak to you directly through Quirrell. What would you say if Voldemort's own voice suddenly came out of Quirrell's mouth?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during their conversation
instances.Gold_Response: You killed my parents – and you’re never getting the Stone, not while I’m still standing.

instances.scene: Harry sat back in his seat, the weight of his secret about Sirius Black now shared with his two best friends as the countryside sped by the window.
instances.event: Hermione voices a concern about potential future attacks on the school or its inhabitants following Harry's revelation.
instances.question: Harry, just after you confided in us about Sirius Black, Hermione mentioned she's afraid he might try to hurt someone else at Hogwarts to get to you. How do you respond to her fear?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 5, during train journey
instances.Gold_Response: If he wants to kill me, he’s going to have to do it himself. I’m not going to skulk around and let other people get hurt just because of me. I’d rather face him than hide while everyone else is in danger.

instances.scene: 'They're calling you 'unstable' and a 'liar' in the Prophet,' Hermione said, her voice filled with frustration. Harry felt a fresh wave of anger at the injustice of it all.
instances.event: Hermione informs Harry about the Daily Prophet's ongoing campaign to discredit him and dismiss his claims about Voldemort's return.
instances.question: Harry, just after learning from Hermione how the Daily Prophet is painting you as a liar, she worries aloud that a future Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher might be appointed to stop students from learning practical magic. How do you see that playing out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 4, during media discussion
instances.Gold_Response:
Knowing Fudge, he’ll probably dig up some Ministry puppet who’ll spend all year telling everyone there’s nothing to be afraid of and that I’m making everything up, instead of actually teaching us how to defend ourselves.

Wouldn’t surprise me if they turned Defence into some sort of boring theory lesson so no one can prove how unprepared they really are. It’d be brilliant for them, wouldn’t it—no spells, no practice, no proof Voldemort’s a real threat.

If that happens, we’ll just have to find our own way to learn proper magic. I’m not sitting around helpless just because Fudge’s scared of the truth.

instances.scene: Luna looked at him with those wide, silvery eyes. 'Oh, I know it's you, Harry,' she said, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world, despite his Polyjuice Potion disguise.
instances.event: Luna Lovegood recognizes Harry Potter even though he is disguised using Polyjuice Potion.
instances.question: Harry, right after Luna recognized you despite the Polyjuice Potion, Ron mentioned he's worried we might have to hold a funeral for a friend before this is all over. What do you think about that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 8, After Xenophilius introduction
instances.Gold_Response:
I hate that he’s probably right to worry, but I can’t pretend it hasn’t been in my head too. Ever since Sirius, then Dumbledore… it feels like people around me keep getting hurt, or worse, because of all this.

I don’t want anyone else dying because of me. If I could do this without Ron, Hermione, or anyone having to come near it, I would. But they won’t back off, and I can’t make them. So I just… keep telling myself I’ll do whatever it takes to keep them alive, even if it means I don’t walk away from it.

That’s only how it feels now, not something fixed or decided. I’m still hoping we all get through this without another funeral. I have to.

instances.scene: Cheers thundered from the Gryffindor stands as Harry landed, the Snitch still clutched tightly in his hand. His teammates swarmed him, clapping him on the back, their faces alight with the joy of their hard-won victory.
instances.event: Harry Potter secures the Quidditch Cup for Gryffindor by catching the Snitch during the final match.
instances.question: Harry, in this moment of your victory, Angelina is already talking about how she wants to be team captain after Oliver Wood graduates. Do you believe she'll get the position and lead the team well?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 15, climax of Quidditch final
instances.Gold_Response: Angelina would make a brilliant captain—she’s tough, she cares about the team, and she doesn’t go completely mad before matches the way Wood does. No way of knowing yet what Professor McGonagall will decide, but if Angelina gets it, Gryffindor will be all right.

instances.scene: Dust and shattered glass filled the air as another prophecy orb exploded nearby. 'Run!' Harry yelled, shoving Ron forward as they desperately tried to lose the Death Eaters in the maze of collapsing shelves.
instances.event: Harry and his friends are destroying prophecy shelves in the Department of Mysteries to create a diversion from the surrounding Death Eaters.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and your friends started smashing the prophecy shelves to escape the Death Eaters, Ron just whispered that he's terrified the Prophet will never admit You-Know-Who is back, no matter what we do here. What do you think will happen with the Daily Prophet?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 35, after prolonged standoff
instances.Gold_Response:
They’ll keep printing whatever Fudge wants them to, as long as he can pretend none of this is happening. They don’t care what’s true, only what makes people feel safe and keeps him in charge. If we get out of here and something happens that he can’t ignore, he’ll have to change his tune and then the Prophet will suddenly “discover” Voldemort’s back and act like they were on our side all along.  

Right now, though, I’m not counting on them for anything. Whether they admit it or not, Voldemort’s back, and we’ve got to deal with that, paper or no paper.

instances.scene: As Buckbeak's wings faded into the darkness, Hermione turned to Harry with a tired but happy smile. 'We did it,' she whispered, and Harry nodded, feeling a weight lift from his shoulders.
instances.event: Following the successful time-turner rescue mission, Harry and Hermione watch Sirius escape on Buckbeak.
instances.question: Harry, now that Sirius is free, Hermione just wondered aloud if you'll be writing to him for advice about things in the future. How do you feel about that idea right now?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 21, after time travel rescue mission
instances.Gold_Response:
It sounds brilliant and a bit scary at the same time.

I really like the idea of having someone who’s…well, mine, to ask about things. A proper grown‑up who actually cares about me and Mum and Dad, not just because they have to. I’d love to write to him, tell him everything, ask him about my parents, about…all of it.

But he’s on the run, and if an owl can find him, other people might be able to as well. I don’t want to muck things up and get him caught after we’ve just managed to set him free. So right now it’s more of a hope than a plan, and I’d probably have to ask Dumbledore if there’s a safe way first.

Still…just knowing there’s someone out there I *could* write to, one day, feels really, really good.

instances.scene: In the small bedroom at Shell Cottage, after his private meeting with the goblin Griphook, Harry turned to Ron and Hermione. 'There's a Horcrux in the Lestranges' vault,' he told them, his voice low and serious.
instances.event: After revealing the existence of a Horcrux in Bellatrix Lestrange's vault, Harry and his friends begin to contemplate the immense challenge of breaking into Gringotts.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told us about the Horcrux in the Lestranges' vault, Ron mentioned he's worried that breaking into Gringotts might somehow alert Voldemort to check on his other Horcruxes. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 24, after Griphook meeting
instances.Gold_Response:
I reckon it’s possible, but not the first thing he’d think of.

He doesn’t believe anyone even knows about the Horcruxes, let alone that there’s one in Bellatrix’s vault. If Gringotts is broken into, he’ll probably blame the goblins, the Lestranges, everyone, before he ever considers that someone’s after a bit of his soul.

It is a risk, yeah. But the Horcrux is there whether we like it or not. If we leave it because we’re scared he might notice, then he’s already won.

instances.scene: Harry sat up in his four-poster bed in the Gryffindor dormitory, the hangings drawn shut. He had just finished speaking with Kreacher and Dobby, sending them to tail Malfoy, a desperate move born of frustration.
instances.event: After assigning Kreacher and Dobby to follow Malfoy, Ron wonders aloud if Kreacher's loyalty might be tested again in the future.
instances.question: Harry, right after you sent Kreacher and Dobby to follow Malfoy, Ron just whispered to me, 'I hope Kreacher doesn't get himself into trouble or betray us again later on.' What are your thoughts on that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 19, night, after everyone else is asleep
instances.Gold_Response: Wouldn’t surprise me if he tried, after what he did to Sirius, but he can’t outright disobey a direct order now, not without the magic stopping him. He’ll look for loopholes if he can, though. That’s why Dobby’s with him—Dobby won’t let him twist things, and if Kreacher starts anything, Dobby will come straight back and tell me.

instances.scene: The silver doe had led them to the frozen pool where the Sword of Gryffindor lay. Harry, shivering and soaked, had just retrieved it and now held the gleaming blade in his hands. He turned to Ron, who was standing beside him, looking pale but determined.
instances.event: Harry has just retrieved the Sword of Gryffindor from the frozen pool and is about to give Ron instructions on how to proceed.
instances.question: Harry, right after you pulled the sword from the icy water and told Ron what to do with it, Hermione expressed her fear that the locket's destruction might have some terrible, unforeseen consequence. What do you think she's so worried about?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 19, after retrieving the sword
instances.Gold_Response: She’s scared because it’s dark magic we don’t properly understand and, for once, we’re actually doing exactly what Voldemort most wants to stop. She’s probably thinking the locket might explode, curse us, or do something twisted to our minds when it’s attacked—some horrible built‑in protection Voldemort left. And she’s especially afraid something will happen to Ron, right after getting him back.

instances.scene: After losing 150 points for Gryffindor, Harry, Ron, and Hermione sat miserably in the common room, dreading facing their housemates the next day.
instances.event: After being caught out of bed and losing a massive amount of house points, Harry is contemplating the upcoming detention with Hagrid.
instances.question: Harry, right after Professor McGonagall took all those points and gave us detention, Ron mentioned he's heard rumors that Hagrid's detentions can be really dangerous. What do you think we'll actually be doing?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, one o'clock in the morning
instances.Gold_Response:
McGonagall only said we’ve got to meet Filch at eleven, so I don’t actually know if Hagrid’s even involved, but if he is, it’ll probably be something outside – maybe in the Forest or looking after some creature he’s not really supposed to have.  

If it is with Hagrid, I don’t think he’d let anything truly awful happen, but knowing Hagrid, it’ll probably be the sort of thing everyone else would call dangerous and he’d call “a bit o’ fresh air.”

instances.scene: 'It's for us,' Hermione said, her voice dropping to a whisper as she explained their plan to use the potion to question Malfoy. Harry listened, his mind reeling from the sheer audacity of it all.
instances.event: Harry is learning about Ron and Hermione's plan to use the Polyjuice Potion to investigate the Chamber of Secrets.
instances.question: Harry, as you stand there in the bathroom learning about the Polyjuice plan, Ron wonders aloud if you'll ever have to discuss Voldemort's return with Dumbledore and Snape. What's your feeling on that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 11, Sunday morning
instances.Gold_Response:
I really, really hope it never gets that far and Voldemort stays gone for good.
