The Ministry thought I’d done magic, the Dursleys were thrilled to have an excuse to lock me up, and Hedwig’s locked in her cage so I can’t even write anyone to explain.

I keep trying to tell myself Dumbledore won’t just forget I exist, that Ron and Hermione will notice when I don’t answer and do something, but lying here with the cat flap in the door and cold soup for dinner, it’s hard not to think I might really be stuck here all summer. Part of me’s still hoping someone from the wizarding world will turn up and sort it all out; another part’s starting to think I might not see Hogwarts again at all.

instances.scene: Mrs. Weasley stood in the doorway of Ron's room, her arms crossed, her expression a mixture of anger and deep concern. 'I want to know what you're planning, Harry. You're throwing away your education!'
instances.event: Shortly after Harry refused to tell Mrs. Weasley about Dumbledore's mission, Ron mentions his mother's emotional state and a future interaction.
instances.question: Harry, right after you couldn't tell Mrs. Weasley about the mission, Ron said to you, 'Mum's really upset. I'm worried she might not even speak to us properly for the rest of the day.' Do you think she'll stay angry with you for long?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 6, shortly before lunch
instances.Gold_Response: No, not for long… not really. She might stay cold with us for the rest of the day, maybe keep fussing over wedding plans to avoid talking about it, but she never stays properly angry forever. She’ll calm down once she’s had time to worry herself out and sees we’re still here and still alive—for now.

instances.scene: Harry stood in Dumbledore's office, the images from the Pensieve still vivid in his mind. 'The Lestranges were sent to Azkaban for torturing the Longbottoms,' Dumbledore said quietly, his eyes full of a sorrowful gravity.
instances.event: After witnessing a memory of a Death Eater trial, Harry learns from Dumbledore that Neville Longbottom's parents were tortured into insanity by Bellatrix Lestrange and others.
instances.question: Harry, just after Dumbledore told you what happened to Neville's parents, Ron mentions he's heard a rumor that Voldemort himself might soon try to return to a physical body. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 29, when Harry asks about the trial he witnessed
instances.Gold_Response:
It doesn’t feel like a rumour at all, it feels like something that’s already happening.

He’s not going to stay the way he is if he can help it – he’s too proud, too…hungry for power. The dream I had before school started, with Wormtail and him talking about getting his body back and using me for something – that didn’t feel like any normal dream. My scar hurt, like it did just now when I saw him in the Pensieve memory, and it keeps hurting more often.

Sirius and Dumbledore are both taking it seriously, and they don’t scare easily. After seeing what those Death Eaters did to Neville’s parents just because they thought they could find their master through them…if they’d do that when You-Know-Who’s gone, I don’t want to imagine what they’ll do if he’s properly back.

So, yeah, I think he’s trying. I’m scared, of course I am, mostly for everyone else, but I don’t think hiding from the idea will stop it. If he’s coming back, I’m going to have to face him again, whether I like it or not.

instances.scene: Staring out his window, Harry couldn't stop turning over the details of that terrible night in Godric's Hollow. The image of his mother and father lying dead was permanently etched in his mind.
instances.event: Harry remembers Voldemort murdering his parents and the mysterious rebounding curse that destroyed the Dark Lord.
instances.question: Harry, right after you finished remembering your parents' murder and how Voldemort's curse backfired, Hermione speculated that if you ever faced Voldemort again, your parents might somehow be able to communicate with you from beyond the grave to help you. How do you respond to that idea?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 2, historical recollection
instances.Gold_Response: I want it to be true so much it actually hurts, but it just isn’t how it works. Dead people don’t come back and start giving you advice in duels, not even for something as big as Voldemort. If Mum and Dad could’ve talked to me, they’d have done it long before now. Dumbledore’s always said no magic can bring back the dead, and my parents aren’t ghosts, so… they’re gone. Maybe there’s some sort of protection left from what Mum did, something Voldemort can’t touch, but that’s not the same as them actually speaking to me. If they help me at all, it’s just by being there in my head, what I remember of them, not… not from beyond the grave.

instances.scene: Walking across the grounds after Hermione had explained Ron's jealousy, Harry felt a heavy weight in his chest.
instances.event: Hermione has just told Harry that Ron is jealous of his attention and fame as a Triwizard champion.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hermione explained Ron's jealousy to you during your Sunday walk, some students are whispering that this rift might get worse and you two could have a huge falling out. What do you think will happen between you and Ron?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Sunday morning walk
instances.Gold_Response:
Ron and I have had rows before, but this one… hurts more.  

Right now I’m too angry and tired to go running after him, especially when he thinks I actually wanted all this. But he’s still my best mate, whether he’s acting like it or not. I don’t want some huge permanent falling out, and I don’t believe he really does either.  

My guess – and it’s only a guess – is that he’ll cool down once he’s had time to think and realise I didn’t put my name in. It might get worse for a bit before that happens, especially with everyone staring and talking, but I can’t see us staying like this forever. At least, I really hope we don’t.

instances.scene: The air filled with crackling heat as monstrous shapes of flame began to form around them, the Fiendfyre spreading with terrifying speed through the Room of Requirement.
instances.event: Crabbe unleashes the cursed fire Fiendfyre in the Room of Requirement, creating a deadly, uncontrollable inferno.
instances.question: Harry, right after Crabbe unleashed the Fiendfyre and we're trying to escape, Ron just shouted that he's worried the whole castle might burn down. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during confrontation
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know if it can get out of the Room of Requirement, but it’s eating everything in here and it’s not stopping. This room’s huge, and if the fire finds a way to spread, it could take the castle with it. 

Right now all I’m sure of is that if we don’t get out on those brooms, it won’t matter what happens to Hogwarts, because we’ll be dead before we see it.

instances.scene: After the Care of Magical Creatures lesson where Hagrid had them walking Blast-Ended Skrewts, Ron and Hermione were discussing Hagrid's odd behaviour. 'He pulled you aside for a private chat, Harry,' said Hermione, looking concerned. 'Do you think he might be planning something dangerous again, like with the dragons last year?'
instances.event: Hagrid secretly invites Harry to meet him at midnight during the Hogsmeade visit to show him the dragons for the first task.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hagrid pulled you aside during that Skrewt-walking lesson, Hermione is worried he might be planning something dangerous. What do you think he's going to ask you to do?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 17, Care of Magical Creatures class
instances.Gold_Response:
He’s definitely up to something, but I don’t reckon he’s going to ask me to *do* anything straight off – more likely he wants to *show* me something he’s not supposed to. Knowing Hagrid, it’ll be some enormous, deadly creature that he thinks is “brilliant” and everyone else thinks is a nightmare.  

My guess is it’s got something to do with the first task, something he thinks will help me, even if the teachers wouldn’t exactly approve. I’m not sure what, but if Hagrid’s asking me to bring the Invisibility Cloak at midnight, it’s got to be secret and probably dangerous. I’m still going.

instances.scene: The cold was intensifying, and Harry felt a familiar, soul-sucking despair. Dudley staggered, his eyes wide with a terror he couldn't comprehend.
instances.event: Dementors attack Harry and Dudley in a dark alleyway, causing them both to experience overwhelming fear and despair.
instances.question: Harry, right after the Dementors attacked you and Dudley in that alley, if Ron had said he was worried you'd have to drag your cousin all the way home, what would you have thought was going to happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 1, night, during the confrontation
instances.Gold_Response: I’d have reckoned I really *would* have to drag him—literally—back to Privet Drive, half-carrying that great lump all the way, trying not to drop my wand or step on him in the dark. I’d be sure no one from the Ministry was going to help, only turn up later to chuck me out of Hogwarts for using magic, and the Dursleys would go spare and blame me for the whole thing anyway. I’d have just thought it was me, Dudley, and a long, miserable haul home with no one else coming to sort it out.

instances.scene: Harry was sitting up, rubbing his chest, taking deep breaths. After being pulled from the frozen pool, he felt the chill slowly leaving him. Ron stood nearby, looking both relieved and apprehensive.
instances.event: Harry has just been saved from drowning by Ron, and they are discussing the mysterious silver doe and Ron's unexpected return.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're safe and talking with Ron about the doe, Hermione mentions she's worried that the sword might be needed again for another Horcrux. Do you think we'll have to use it like this more than once?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 19, after Harry is saved
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I reckon we will. The sword’s the only thing we know for sure can finish them off, like the diary, so unless we find something just as good, we’re going to have to use it on every Horcrux we can get our hands on.

instances.scene: Hagrid handed Harry a large cage containing a beautiful snowy owl. 'Happy birthday, Harry,' he said, beaming.
instances.event: Hagrid buys Harry a snowy owl, Hedwig, as a birthday present during their Diagon Alley shopping trip.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hagrid gave you Hedwig, Ron mentioned he's heard rumors about a break-in at Gringotts and wonders if that mysterious package Hagrid collected might be the target. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, late in Diagon Alley shopping
instances.Gold_Response:
I haven’t heard anything about any break-in at Gringotts. Hagrid said you’d have to be barking mad to try and rob the place, and after seeing all those carts and goblins and everything, I believe him.  

That little package he took from that special vault definitely seemed important, the way he wouldn’t say what it was and kept it close, but he’s doing it for Dumbledore, so I reckon it’s meant to be secret and safe.  

If anyone ever did try to break into Gringotts, I suppose something like that would be exactly what they’d go for—but right now it’s just one more mystery I don’t really understand, and I’m not about to start doubting Hagrid over it.

instances.scene: A heavy silence filled the tent, broken only by their ragged breaths. The shattered remains of Slytherin's locket smoked faintly, the dark magic within it vanquished by the goblin-made blade.
instances.event: Following the destruction of the Horcrux, Harry and Ron are in a moment of respite, the immediate danger passed but the tension of Ron's recent return palpable.
instances.question: Harry, with the locket gone, Ron looks exhausted but relieved. He's just asked if you think the three of you can get back to working together properly now. What's your honest feeling about how things will go from here?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 19, after opening the locket with Parseltongue
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, yeah, I do.  

It’s going to be rough sometimes, and Hermione’s going to be furious at you for a bit, but that’s between you and her.  

As far as I’m concerned, you’re back, we’ve destroyed the Horcrux, and I trust you. If we stick together and actually say what’s going on instead of stewing about it, we’ll be all right.

instances.scene: The plan was set. They would enter the Ministry tomorrow. As they prepared for the night, a tense silence fell over the tent, each of them lost in their own thoughts about the dangers ahead.
instances.event: After the plan is made, Hermione voices a fear that the Ministry might already be aware they are coming, raising the possibility of a trap.
instances.question: Harry, right after we all agreed to your plan for the Ministry, Hermione just whispered that she's afraid they might already know we're coming and will be waiting for us. How do you think they'll first realize we're inside?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 12, evening
instances.Gold_Response: Most likely it’ll be something small we get wrong. If anyone at the visitor entrance recognises one of the people we’re pretending to be, or asks a question we can’t answer, that could be it. They’re checking wands now, so if they’ve got any way of matching wands to owners, that’s another risk. Or one of the real Ministry people we’re impersonating could turn up unexpectedly and blow everything. At this point, it feels less like they’ll “sense” us going in and more that we’ll give ourselves away if we slip, so all we can do is be convincing enough that no one looks closely until we’ve done what we came to do.

instances.scene: Harry stood frozen, ropes binding him tightly as Quirrell paced before him. 'I let the troll in, you know,' Quirrell said calmly, 'as a diversion.'
instances.event: After revealing he let the troll into Hogwarts, Quirrell continues to interrogate Harry while he is magically bound.
instances.question: Harry, right after Quirrell confessed to letting the troll into Hogwarts and while you're still bound by his magical ropes, Ron whispers to you that he's afraid Quirrell might try to possess someone else next. What do you tell him?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during interrogation of Harry
instances.Gold_Response: “Ron, don’t—don’t even say that now. He’s not getting the Stone, that’s what matters. Just stall him if you can, and Dumbledore will come. He won’t have time to try anything like that.”

instances.scene: 'He's just trying to get a rise out of you,' Hermione said, as they walked back from the Hog's Head. 'But he did raise a point about the risk. What if someone tells Umbridge?' Ron scoffed, 'No one would.'
instances.event: Following the meeting, the trio discusses the risks and Zacharias Smith's skepticism.
instances.question: Harry, in the aftermath of the Hog's Head meeting where Ron stood up for you, Ron confidently says he doesn't think anyone will betray the group to Umbridge. Do you share his confidence, or are you worried someone might?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 16, during the Hog's Head meeting
instances.Gold_Response:
I’m nowhere near as sure as Ron is.

I want to believe everyone who turned up today is on our side – they looked it, when they were listening, and when they signed. And it meant a lot, seeing how many were willing to be there after everything the Prophet’s been saying about me.

But after what happened with my parents and Pettigrew, and with the Ministry twisting everything, it’s hard not to imagine someone getting scared, or their parents finding out, or Umbridge putting pressure on them. Zacharias Smith already annoys me enough that I can picture him running his mouth, even if he didn’t mean to betray us properly.

So I hope Ron’s right – I really do – but I can’t feel as relaxed about it as he does. It’s just a hope at the moment, not something I’m certain of.

instances.scene: Harry lay on the ground, writhing in pain as the Cruciatus Curse washed over him. Voldemort stood over him, his high, cold laugh echoing in the graveyard.
instances.event: Voldemort has just tortured Harry with the Cruciatus Curse and is now toying with him before their duel.
instances.question: Harry, right after Voldemort stops torturing you with the Cruciatus Curse, Ron's voice echoes in your mind, 'He's going to kill you! He said he would!' What do you think will happen next?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 32, after explaining his return
instances.Gold_Response:
He’s going to kill me, of course he is. That’s what all of this has been for. But not quickly. He’ll want to play with me first, hurt me again, show off in front of his Death Eaters, make me beg.  

I can’t let him have that. If he unties me, if I get even the smallest chance, I’ve got to try to fight him or get to the cup. I’ll probably die here, but if I’m going to, it’ll be on my feet with my wand in my hand, not whimpering at his feet.

instances.scene: The basin was now half-empty. Dumbledore drank, and then drank again, each swallow seeming more painful than the last. 'Keep going, Professor,' Harry said, his voice strained with anxiety.
instances.event: Harry watches as Dumbledore continues drinking the painful potion, forcing himself to help the Headmaster through the ordeal.
instances.question: Harry, while Dumbledore is still drinking that awful potion, Hermione just asked if you think you'll be able to get him water afterwards when he's suffering. What's your plan for helping him once he finishes?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 26, after deciding to drink potion
instances.Gold_Response: I’ll get him water with magic—Aguamenti into the goblet, straight to his mouth if I have to—and if that doesn’t work, I’ll use the lake, even if I have to lean right out over it and scoop it up myself. I’ll keep hold of him, make him drink till he’s better able to stand, and then I’m getting him out of here as fast as I can. I’m not leaving him to suffer in this place, whatever I have to do.

instances.scene: Harry and Cedric stood panting before the Triwizard Cup, its glow illuminating their determined faces. 'We'll take it at the same time,' Harry said firmly. 'It's still a Hogwarts victory.'
instances.event: Harry and Cedric agree to take the Triwizard Cup together, deciding to share the victory as Hogwarts champions.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Cedric agreed to grab the Triwizard Cup together, Ron mentioned he's worried the Cup might be a trap that transports you somewhere dangerous. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 30, during maze task at the cup
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, that hadn’t really occurred to me until you said it.  

Everything about this tournament’s been off from the start—my name coming out of the Goblet, the dragons, the way Moody’s been on at me all year—so I can’t say it’s impossible there’s something dodgy about the Cup as well. It could be a trap; it wouldn’t be the strangest thing that’s happened to me.  

But Dumbledore’s here, all the judges are here, the whole school’s watching… you’d think they’d have checked the Cup for anything like that. It’s supposed to be the finish line. And right now, after that spider and everything else in this maze, it honestly looks like the safest option we’ve got.  

So, yeah, I’m a bit suspicious of everything at this point, but if it is a trap, I don’t see what else Cedric and I can do except take it together and be ready to deal with whatever’s waiting on the other end—if there is anything.

instances.scene: A heavy gloom had settled over the tent following the news from Potterwatch, the weight of each new loss pressing down on them.
instances.event: Following the broadcast, Harry speaks Voldemort's name, triggering the Taboo and leading to their imminent confrontation with the Snatchers.
instances.question: Harry, just after we turned off the radio and before you broke the Taboo, Hermione wondered aloud if we'd ever find another safe place like Grimmauld Place. Do you think we'll find another secret headquarters for the Order?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 22, after Potterwatch broadcast
instances.Gold_Response: I hope so, but I honestly don’t know. The Order’s probably got other hideouts, but Grimmuald was meant to be the place, and look how that turned out once Snape and Yaxley were in on it. Anywhere fixed feels dangerous now; staying on the move might be the only real safety we’ve got. If there is another headquarters somewhere, it’ll be up to the Order to use it—we can’t plan on anyone swooping in to give us a new safe house, not with what we’ve got to do.

instances.scene: Harry was sitting up in his hospital bed, the events in the chambers below the trapdoor finally settling in his mind. Dumbledore had just explained how his mother's loving sacrifice had left a powerful protection in his very skin, which was why Quirrell couldn't touch him.
instances.event: After the confrontation with Quirrell and Voldemort, Dumbledore visits Harry in the hospital wing and explains the magical protection Harry carries from his mother's sacrifice.
instances.question: Harry, just after Dumbledore explained why Quirrell couldn't touch you, Ron mentioned he's worried that Voldemort might try to come back to Hogwarts next year with some new, terrible plan. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 17, during hospital wing conversation
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t see why he’d give up just because he failed once, so I suppose he might try something again, maybe even here. But Hogwarts is still the safest place I know, and Dumbledore’s not exactly easy to get past. 

If Voldemort does come back with some new plan, I’d rather be here with Ron and Hermione and Dumbledore than anywhere else. I am a bit scared, but I’m not going to spend the whole summer jumping at shadows, and I’m certainly not going to run away from Hogwarts.

instances.scene: Walking back from the Great Hall, Ron was fuming. 'Did you hear what Malfoy called Hermione? That foul little...' Harry nodded grimly, his own anger simmering.
instances.event: After Draco Malfoy insults Hermione with a racial slur, Ron expresses his outrage to Harry.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy insulted Hermione, Ron mutters, 'I bet Krum's going to invite her to visit Bulgaria over the summer after all this. What do you think?'
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 22, evening after leaving Great Hall
instances.Gold_Response: Knowing Hermione, she’d only say yes if he agreed to spend the whole summer in a library. Anyway, loads of girls are chasing Krum, he probably doesn’t even know who she is — Malfoy’s just trying to wind you up.

instances.scene: The shockwave from the blast knocked Harry into the wall. Through the settling dust, he saw the aftermath of the explosion.
instances.event: Fred Weasley is killed by an explosion during the Battle of Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, in this moment of chaos just after the explosion, Hermione whispers that she fears we might not be able to properly honor the fallen until this is all over. How do you see things playing out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 31, during battle
instances.Gold_Response:
We can’t stop now, not for anything, or there’ll only be more of them to honour.

If we make it through this, really through it, then we’ll have time to say all the things they deserve, to sit with them properly, to tell the whole world what they did here. That’s how I see it, or how I have to see it.

But right now the only way to honour Fred – everyone – is to finish this, to get to Voldemort, to end it, so there aren’t any more bodies lined up beside his.

instances.scene: Harry sat at the Gryffindor table, reading the letter from Sirius that had just arrived by owl, his mind racing about the arranged meeting.
instances.event: Harry receives a warning letter from Sirius Black about the danger at Hogwarts, which happens later in the story.
instances.question: Harry, right after you received Sirius's letter arranging a meeting, Ron mentioned he's worried Sirius might send another letter warning you about some specific danger at Hogwarts. What would you say to him?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 26, Friday morning breakfast
instances.Gold_Response: I don’t want him to send anything unless he absolutely has to. Every letter’s another chance for him to be spotted, isn’t it? If something’s going to happen, I’m probably safer here with Dumbledore than anywhere else. And it’s not like trouble ever has much trouble finding me, Hogwarts or no Hogwarts.

instances.scene: In the tense quiet following their escape, Hermione pulled out her charmed bag. 'I've been packing for days, Harry,' she said, a slight tremor in her voice. 'Clothes, books, your Invisibility Cloak... everything I thought we might need.' They stood under the dim streetlights, the weight of their new reality settling upon them.
instances.event: Harry Potter learns the extent of Hermione's preparations for their horcrux hunt immediately after they flee the wedding, highlighting her foresight and the precariousness of their situation.
instances.question: Harry, now that we've seen what Hermione packed and we're hiding out here, she just mentioned she's afraid our magical signatures might be traceable now that the Ministry has fallen. She's predicting we could be ambushed at any moment, even in a public place. How are you feeling about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 9, after arriving on Tottenham Court Road
instances.Gold_Response:
It’s like having a wand at your back you can’t see.

I’m jumpy, I suppose, but not exactly surprised. Ever since the wedding was attacked it’s felt like they’re right on top of us anyway. If Hermione says they might be able to track us, I have to take that seriously, even if the idea of being ambushed in the middle of a Muggle café feels wrong, somehow.

Mostly I’m angry that we’re already this exposed and we’ve barely started. But if they do come, at least it’s clear what to do: keep Ron and Hermione alive, fight if we have to, and get out. Sitting here waiting is the worst part.

instances.scene: Firenze galloped through the dark forest, Harry on his back, having just fled from the hooded figure drinking unicorn blood. 'It is a monstrous thing, to slay a unicorn,' Firenze said, his voice echoing in the quiet woods. 'The blood will keep you alive, even if you are an inch from death, but at a terrible price.'
instances.event: After being rescued by the centaur Firenze from a hooded figure in the Forbidden Forest, Harry is carried to safety while Firenze explains the dark magic of unicorn blood and hints at Voldemort's presence.
instances.question: Harry, right after Firenze rescued you from that terrifying hooded figure in the forest and is carrying you to safety, Ron mentions he's heard rumors that this centaur might one day become a Hogwarts professor. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, during forest search
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, after what he just did for me, I’d trust Firenze more than half the adults at Hogwarts.

It’d be a bit strange having a centaur at the staff table, but he’s calm, knows loads about the forest and the stars, and he actually seems to care if I stay alive, which is more than I can say for Snape. If he became a professor, I’d probably feel safer, not less.

instances.scene: The fire crackled in the Gryffindor common room as Oliver Wood finished explaining his concerns about the dementors. 'We can't have a repeat of last time, Harry. We need to be prepared.'
instances.event: Oliver Wood seeks out Harry to develop a strategy for dealing with dementors during Quidditch matches, expressing his determination to win the Cup.
instances.question: Harry, just after your conversation with Wood about protecting the team from dementors, Hermione wonders if you'll actually catch the Snitch to win the final match and have Dumbledore personally present the Cup. How do you respond to her speculation?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 12, night before term starts
instances.Gold_Response:
If I catch the Snitch and we actually win the Cup, that’d be amazing enough on its own—having Dumbledore hand it to us would just be… well, unbelievable.  

But right now I’m more worried about not falling off my broom again. If I can get the Patronus strong enough, maybe the dementors won’t matter and we’ll have a real chance. That’s just what I’m hoping, though—I’ve no clue how it’ll really go.

instances.scene: Stumbling onto the dark beach, Harry released Dobby's hand. 'We're safe,' he panted, looking around at the shadowy outlines of his friends and the goblin.
instances.event: The group has just successfully escaped Malfoy Manor and arrived at a safe location with Dobby.
instances.question: Harry, now that you're safe on this beach after Dobby rescued you all from the cellar, Hermione whispers that she's afraid Bellatrix might find a way to retaliate against Dobby specifically. How do you respond?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 23, during escape
instances.Gold_Response: She’s not touching him again. We’re out, she’s still stuck back there, and house-elf magic got us clean away right under her nose. If she could chase him, she’d be here already. Dobby’s with us now, and I’ll make bloody sure Bellatrix Lestrange never gets near him again.

instances.scene: Hagrid had just confirmed to Harry, Ron, and Hermione that he and Madame Maxime had been on a secret mission to find the giants. He looked exhausted and injured, but proud of their efforts.
instances.event: After Hagrid reveals his mission to the giants, a friend expresses concern about the potential long-term consequences of this mission.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hagrid told you and your friends about his mission to the giants, Ron mentioned he was worried Hagrid might try to bring one of them back to Hogwarts someday. What did you think about that possibility at the time?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 20, after pressure from trio
instances.Gold_Response: It sounded completely mental, even for Hagrid, so at first I sort of brushed it off as Ron being Ron. But knowing Hagrid, and how he gets about dangerous creatures, there was this horrible little feeling that he *might* actually try something like that if he thought it was the right thing to do. I was mostly just hoping Dumbledore would never let it happen, and that Hagrid had had such a rough time with the giants he’d know better than to bring one anywhere near the school.

instances.scene: Looking around at the gathered fighters in the Room of Requirement, Harry felt a surge of hope despite the danger ahead.
instances.event: Harry assesses the situation after finding reinforcements in the Room of Requirement before the final battle.
instances.question: Harry, now that we're all gathered here in the Room of Requirement preparing for battle, Ginny just expressed concern that some of the people in this room might be among the casualties. How do you respond to that fear?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 30, after leaving McGonagall
instances.Gold_Response:
I hate that she’s right.

I’d tell her I don’t want a single one of them hurt, that I’d give anything for all of them to be on a train miles away from here. But they’ve chosen to stay, same as she has, and trying to pretend there won’t be casualties won’t help anyone.

So I’d say we’re going to make every second count. We’re going to fight smart, stick together, watch each other’s backs, and do everything we can to make sure it’s them, not us, who falls. And I’d promise her that as long as I’m alive, I’ll do whatever I can to keep her and the others breathing.

I can’t swear everyone will walk out of this. But I can swear Voldemort’s not taking this castle without a fight he’ll never forget.

instances.scene: The warm, smoky atmosphere of Hagrid's hut, with Slughorn becoming increasingly sentimental over mead while Harry watches for an opportunity.
instances.event: Harry is waiting for the right moment during the drinking session to confront Slughorn about the suppressed memory of Lily Potter's death.
instances.question: Harry, while you're here in Hagrid's hut sharing drinks, Hermione just whispered that she thinks Slughorn might actually give you that important memory before the night is over. How confident are you that he'll hand it over?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 22, night after burial
instances.Gold_Response: Pretty confident, to be honest—more than I’d usually be about anything to do with Slughorn. The Felix is working, you can feel it, and he’s in exactly the mood I was hoping for. But until he actually hands the memory over, it’s only a strong hope, not a sure thing.

instances.scene: Ron was holding the tiny owl, looking both pleased and a bit sad about Scabbers, as he finished reading Sirius's note.
instances.event: Sirius sends Ron a new pet owl to make up for the loss of Scabbers, who was revealed to be Peter Pettigrew.
instances.question: Harry, now that Sirius has sent Ron a new owl, Hermione mentioned she's concerned Professor Lupin might not be the only one leaving Hogwarts soon. What's your feeling about other staff changes?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 22, while reading Sirius's letter
instances.Gold_Response:
I hate the idea of anyone else leaving, to be honest. Lupin going is bad enough.

I’m not really worried about Hagrid now Buckbeak’s… well, safe, even if the Ministry thinks otherwise. And I can’t imagine Hogwarts without Dumbledore or McGonagall or Hagrid; it just doesn’t feel possible. If Fudge tried anything, Dumbledore would stand up to him. He always does.

The only job I’m properly nervous about is Defence Against the Dark Arts. That post seems jinxed, and I’ve no idea who they’ll dig up next. But right now, as far as I actually *know*, it’s only Lupin who’s leaving. The rest is just us lot worrying on the train.

instances.scene: After successfully resisting the Imperius Curse under Professor Moody's instruction, Harry was discussing the lesson with Ron and Hermione in the common room.
instances.event: Following the Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson where Moody taught resisting the Imperius Curse, Ron expresses concern about Moody's intense teaching methods.
instances.question: Harry, after that Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson where Moody taught us to resist the Imperius Curse, Ron just mentioned he's worried Moody's methods might get us into serious danger later this year. What do you think might happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 14, During Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know exactly what’ll happen, but it feels like Moody’s getting us ready for something real, not just exams. After the World Cup and my scar hurting, it doesn’t seem impossible we might actually need to know how to fight curses like that.

Yeah, he’s a bit mad, and what he did in class was dangerous, but Dumbledore trusts him, so I don’t think he’s going to throw us into something for no reason. If we do end up in serious danger this year, my guess is it’ll be because something dark is coming anyway, and Moody’s just trying to make sure we’re not helpless when it arrives.

instances.scene: Sitting in the train compartment, the weight of his secret now shared with his two best friends, Harry felt a mix of relief and dread. The mention of Sirius Black's name still hung heavily in the air.
instances.event: Harry later reveals to Ron and Hermione that he hears his mother screaming when Dementors are near.
instances.question: Harry, back on the train after you first told us Sirius Black was after you, Hermione wondered if the Dementors guarding the school might affect you more personally than just making you feel cold. How would you have responded to her concern then?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 3, Chapter 5, during train journey
instances.Gold_Response:
I’d have told her to stop worrying so much and that I was fine, really.

I’d probably say something like, “Look, it was just the shock. No one’s ever had one of those things that close to them before, have they? I’m not going to spend the whole year keeling over every time one comes near.”

And if she brought up Black, I’d say, “The Dementors are here for him, not me. If they make me feel a bit worse than other people, I’ll just have to deal with it. I’m not going to let them – or Black – scare me into hiding in a corner.”

instances.scene: Ollivander had just explained how wand allegiance could change through conquest, a concept that was new and troubling to Harry as he considered his own wand's history.
instances.event: Following Ollivander's explanation about wand allegiance changing through conquest, Hermione speculates on the potential consequences for Harry's own wand.
instances.question: Harry, right after Ollivander finished explaining that a wand's loyalty can be won by defeating its previous owner, Hermione is theorizing that this could mean your own wand's allegiance might be challenged in a future duel. How do you see this playing out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 24, during Elder Wand discussion
instances.Gold_Response:
If what Ollivander says is right, then, yeah, if someone overpowers me and takes my wand, it might decide it prefers them. That’s what it sounded like happened with Malfoy and the hawthorn wand.

But my wand’s already done something I don’t understand with Voldemort, that golden fire thing, and Ollivander didn’t really have an answer for that. So my guess – and it’s only a guess – is that there’s more going on between me and my wand than just who snatches it in a duel.

If it comes to it, I’ll use whatever wand I have to. I’m not planning on letting anyone win my wand off me, and if they do, I’ll just have to find another way to beat them. The wand choosing the wizard doesn’t change what I’ve got to do.

instances.scene: After the meeting at the Hog's Head, Ron was fuming. 'That Zacharias Smith! Questioning you like that, as if you were lying about You-Know-Who!'
instances.event: Ron defends Harry against Zacharias Smith's accusations during the initial D.A. meeting.
instances.question: Harry, right after Ron defended you against Zacharias Smith's accusations at the Hog's Head, Hermione mentions she's worried the Ministry might find out about these secret meetings and expel you. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 16, during the Hog's Head meeting
instances.Gold_Response:
If the Ministry finds out, they’ll probably kick up a massive fuss and try to shut us down, maybe even threaten to chuck me out again if they can twist it enough. Fudge is desperate to make me look mad or dangerous, and Umbridge would love an excuse.

But Dumbledore’s still Headmaster, and they haven’t managed to get rid of him, no matter how much they want to. As long as we’re careful, meet somewhere they don’t know about, and don’t go blabbing, I don’t see how they can prove anything. Hermione’s right to worry, but doing nothing just because Fudge’s scared of his own shadow isn’t an option.

So, honestly, I think they might try something if they ever find out—but I’m not planning on giving them the chance.

instances.scene: Walking back to Privet Drive after the dementor attack, Mrs. Figg had just explained that Dumbledore had ordered her to keep an eye on Harry.
instances.event: Mrs. Figg reveals she is a Squib and has been watching Harry on Dumbledore's orders.
instances.question: Harry, right after Mrs. Figg told you Dumbledore had her watching you, Ron mentioned he's worried that you might be expelled from Hogwarts for using magic. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 2, while walking back to Privet Drive
instances.Gold_Response:
I’m scared stiff they’re going to chuck me out, to be honest. The Ministry already warned me once, and now they’ve got an excuse handed to them on a plate.

But I had to do it. There were Dementors in Little Whinging, for Merlin’s sake. If they care at all about the law they’re always going on about, they’ll have to see it was self‑defence.

I’m hanging on to the idea that Dumbledore won’t just sit there and let them expel me. He’s had Mrs. Figg watching me all this time; he must’ve expected something could happen. I keep telling myself he’ll sort it out… but right now it feels like everything’s stacked against me, and I honestly don’t know which way it’ll go.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room after successfully securing his date with Cho, Harry was feeling optimistic when Ron commented, 'At least you won't have to talk about Cedric on your date, right?'
instances.event: Harry is looking forward to his upcoming Valentine's Day date with Cho Chang after inviting her.
instances.question: Harry, Ron just joked that your date with Cho will be great as long as you avoid talking about Cedric. Before your actual Valentine's Day outing, do you think Cedric will come up in your conversation with her?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 24, day after return to Hogwarts
instances.Gold_Response: Yeah, I reckon he probably will, and that’s exactly what I’m dreading, but I don’t see how we can really avoid talking about him at some point.

instances.scene: Harry sat in Professor Moody's office, the door having just clicked shut. Moody fixed him with his magical eye. 'Potter,' he growled, 'I overheard your little chat with Diggory about the egg. You told him about the dragons. Now, I've got a question for you.'
instances.event: Moody has just summoned Harry to his office to discuss Harry's decision to help Cedric Diggory with the first task.
instances.question: Harry, right after Moody summoned you to his office about helping Cedric, Ron mentioned he's worried that Moody might secretly help you again in the next task. What would you say to him?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 19, Monday morning
instances.Gold_Response:
Ron, I didn’t ask Moody to help me, he just hauled me into his office and started talking about “playing to my strengths.” And it’s not like the others aren’t getting help – Hagrid showed me the dragons, but Madame Maxime was there with Fleur, and Karkaroff had Krum there too. I only told Cedric so it would be fair.

I don’t want Moody sneaking me answers for every task. I don’t even like that people already think I cheated my way into this. I just don’t want to get killed in front of the whole school. If there’s a next task and he tries to shove help at me again, I’ll try to figure things out myself first. I want to win fair, or not at all – I just don’t want to die doing it.

instances.scene: In the silent, sleeping Gryffindor common room, Harry was trying to process the terrifying events of the night.
instances.event: Harry has just relayed his vision to Professor McGonagall and is awaiting further news about Mr. Weasley.
instances.question: Harry, in the hours after you told Professor McGonagall about your vision of the snake attack, Hermione sits with you. She looks worried and says, 'If Mr. Weasley pulls through, do you think this will change the Order's strategy? Will Dumbledore start having you train to block these visions?' What is your response?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, late night/early morning
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know what it’ll do to the Order’s plans, Hermione. They’ll probably all start treating me like I’m some sort of… weapon, after what Moody said.  

As for Dumbledore… he won’t even look at me, let alone tell me what he’s planning. Maybe he’ll want me to block the visions if he thinks Voldemort can use me, but the visions just saved Mr Weasley’s life.  

So it could go either way, really. That’s just my guess, though. I’ve no idea what Dumbledore’s actually going to do, because he won’t bloody talk to me.

instances.scene: 'It's too risky,' Harry said, his voice final. Hermione sighed, looking at the potion with frustration, while Ron shuffled his feet uncomfortably.
instances.event: Harry Potter, having just refused the Polyjuice Potion plan, is asked about the future success of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes after the war.
instances.question: Harry, in the moments following your refusal to go along with the Polyjuice plan, Fred joked that he hopes their joke shop will still be standing when this is all over. Do you believe Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes will make it through the war?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 4, after plan explanation
instances.Gold_Response: I really hope it does. Fred and George are too bloody stubborn to let a bunch of Death Eaters shut them down, and people need their jokes now more than ever. Diagon Alley’s getting more dangerous, so anything could happen, but if any shop can survive this mess, it’s theirs—at least, that’s what I’m hanging on to right now, just a hope, not something I actually know.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room, after Harry had returned from detention and later stumbled upon Ron's secret Quidditch practice, the two boys sat together, the cuts on Harry's hand still visible.
instances.event: Harry has discovered Ron's Quidditch practice, and Ron has just noticed the injuries on Harry's hand from Umbridge's detention.
instances.question: Harry, after Ron saw your injured hand tonight, he muttered that Umbridge is going to cause even more trouble for you this year. How do you see this playing out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 13, Thursday evening after detention
instances.Gold_Response:
She hates me. That much is obvious.

She’s not going to stop at a few detentions and a sliced-up hand – she’s here to shut me up about Voldemort, and as long as I keep saying he’s back, she’ll keep coming after me. She’ll probably try to make my life so miserable I either crack or get chucked out of Hogwarts, and she’ll use any rule or new decree she can invent to do it.

But I’m not going to start pretending Voldemort isn’t back just because some Ministry toad in a pink cardigan tells me to. If that means more detentions, losing points, or getting on the wrong side of half the staff, then fine. She can make things harder, but she can’t make me lie.

So yeah, Ron’s right, this is going to get worse. How exactly, I don’t know yet — more detentions, maybe banning me from Quidditch, trying to turn people against me, whatever Fudge thinks up next. But I’m not backing down just because she wants me quiet.

instances.scene: The shop was very small and empty except for a single, spindly chair. Mr. Ollivander was standing behind the counter, his wide, pale eyes shining like moons through the gloom of the shop. 'Curious indeed how these things happen. The wand chooses the wizard, remember... I think we must expect great things from you, Mr. Potter... After all, He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named did great things — terrible, yes, but great.'
instances.event: Harry Potter has just purchased his wand from Ollivander, who revealed its brother-wand connection to Voldemort.
instances.question: Harry, right after Ollivander told you about your wand's connection to Voldemort, Ron wonders aloud if you might ever be captured and end up in a cellar with Ollivander as a fellow prisoner. What would you say to that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 5, final shop visit in Diagon Alley
instances.Gold_Response:
Blimey, Ron, could you pick something a bit less cheerful?

I’ve only just got my wand, I’m not planning on getting captured by anyone, thanks. If You-Know-Who really is gone, then it shouldn’t matter that our wands are connected, should it?

Anyway, if I ever do end up in a cellar with Mr. Ollivander, I hope it’s because we took a wrong turn, not because some dark wizard put us there. But that’s just you imagining things. I’m going to Hogwarts to learn magic, not to get locked up.

instances.scene: The Room of Requirement was buzzing with quiet excitement as the first meeting of Dumbledore's Army concluded. Students were filing out, whispering about the successful practice.
instances.event: After the first D.A. meeting, Hermione expresses concern about how the group will communicate secretly for future meetings.
instances.question: Harry, as everyone leaves the Room of Requirement after our first successful D.A. meeting, Hermione mentions she's worried about how we'll safely alert everyone for the next meeting without Umbridge finding out. What's your thought on that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 18, 8 PM on the seventh floor
instances.Gold_Response: It’s dodgy, yeah. We can’t risk another parchment or poster lying around where Filch or Umbridge could get it, and owls are probably being watched. For now we can pass it on in person—common rooms, corridors, at meals—make sure everyone knows to keep their mouths shut and only talk when it’s safe. You usually come up with the clever plans for this sort of thing anyway, so let’s get back to the common room and you can tell us if you think of something better.

instances.scene: As they walked back to the castle, Hermione frowned thoughtfully. 'Harry, the way Rita Skeeter keeps appearing where she shouldn't be... I'm starting to wonder if she has some secret way of gathering information that we haven't figured out yet.'
instances.event: Hermione speculates to Harry that Rita Skeeter might have an undiscovered method of obtaining information shortly after Skeeter interviewed Hagrid.
instances.question: Harry, just after you saw Rita Skeeter arrange that interview with Hagrid during class, Hermione mentions she suspects Skeeter has some secret way of getting information. How do you think she manages to be everywhere at once?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 20, during Care of Magical Creatures class
instances.Gold_Response:
She’s like a bad Galleon – turns up everywhere you don’t want her.  

Honestly, I’ve got no idea how she does it. Could be some spell for eavesdropping, or an Invisibility Cloak, or a whole bunch of people sneaking her information. Hermione’s sure she’s using something sneaky and magical, some sort of way of bugging people, and she’s usually right about that sort of thing.  

All I know is, whenever there’s something private going on, Skeeter somehow slithers in and twists it.

instances.scene: In the dark, dusty cellar of Malfoy Manor, Harry, Ron, and Hermione huddled together after being captured. They had just discovered the other prisoners: Luna Lovegood, Dean Thomas, the goblin Griphook, and an old, frail-looking Mr. Ollivander.
instances.event: Ollivander later identifies the wands Harry took from Malfoy Manor and explains that wand allegiance can change through conquest.
instances.question: Harry, while you're all trapped here in the Malfoys' cellar with Mr. Ollivander, Ron whispers to you that he hopes the wands we took from the Death Eaters might be useful later. What do you think about that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 23, after Bellatrix takes command
instances.Gold_Response: If we ever see those wands again, I’m bloody well hanging on to them. The blackthorn one worked, even if it never felt quite right, and right now I’d take anything that’ll cast a decent Stunning Spell. I don’t know why some wands seem to work better for us than others, but I’d rather be using a Death Eater’s wand than sitting here wandless. First we’ve got to get out of this cellar, though—then we can worry about whose wand belongs to who.

instances.scene: Slughorn's face had hardened. 'I don't know anything about Horcruxes and I wouldn't tell you if I did!' he shouted. 'Now get out of here at once!'
instances.event: Horace Slughorn angrily rejects Harry Potter's inquiry about Horcruxes, refusing to provide any information on the subject.
instances.question: Harry, right after Slughorn shouted at you and refused to talk about Horcruxes, Ron mentioned he's worried Professor Dumbledore might be targeted with poison at the upcoming birthday celebration in Slughorn's office. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 18, immediately after Harry asks about Horcruxes
instances.Gold_Response:
With everything that’s happened this year, especially that cursed necklace that was clearly meant for Dumbledore, I’d be mad not to take that seriously.

I don’t really believe Slughorn himself is trying to kill Dumbledore – he’s a coward, not a Death Eater, and he cares far too much about staying on the winning side. But he’s got access to loads of rare potions and drinks, and he throws these little parties and sends things round as gifts. That makes him an easy person to use, or to tamper with.

If Dumbledore were going to be drinking anything that had passed through Slughorn’s hands, in his office or anywhere else, I’d be watching it very closely. After what I’ve seen Malfoy up to, I’m sure someone’s still trying to get to Dumbledore inside the castle, and poison would fit perfectly with that.

instances.scene: In the Lovegood house, Xenophilius had just confessed his terrible bargain: the Death Eaters had taken Luna, and he had tried to trade Harry for her. The trio was reeling from this revelation.
instances.event: After Xenophilius Lovegood confesses he tried to trade Harry Potter to Death Eaters in exchange for his captured daughter, Luna.
instances.question: Harry, right after Xenophilius confessed about trying to trade you for Luna, Ron mentioned he's worried the Death Eaters might start targeting the families of other students at Hogwarts next. What do you think will happen?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 21, after Harry confronts him about Luna's absence
instances.Gold_Response:
If they’ve taken Luna to force her dad into line, they’ll do it to others, too. Ron’s right to worry; going after families is exactly the sort of thing Voldemort and his lot would do, especially if they think it’ll flush me out.

I don’t know who they’ll choose or how far they’ll go, but it’s not going to get better while he’s in charge. The only thing that makes any sense is to stay out of their hands and finish what Dumbledore wanted me to do as fast as we can, so they don’t have any more time to hurt people because of me.

instances.scene: The sounds of battle echoed through the corridors. Harry clutched the vial containing Snape's memories, his mind racing with questions about Dumbledore, Snape, and the path ahead.
instances.event: Harry possesses Snape's memories but has not yet viewed them, leaving his immediate future actions and the outcome of the battle uncertain.
instances.question: Harry, at this moment, holding Snape's memories but before you've seen what's in them, Ron suggests that Voldemort's ultimatum means he's about to personally enter the fight. How do you see this playing out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 7, Chapter 32, during battle, after Snape's injury
instances.Gold_Response:
He won’t charge in swinging his wand around, not yet. He likes other people to do the dirty work while he waits somewhere safe, certain he’s already won. That ultimatum’s just to scare everyone and smoke me out, make them turn on me if I don’t show.

He’ll stay back with the snake and the Death Eaters, keep hammering the castle with giants and Dementors, and wait for me to come to him. Sooner or later it’ll still end up with just him and me, but he’ll try to make sure it’s on his terms, not ours.

instances.scene: In the hospital wing, Harry gently unclenched Hermione's stiff fingers and found a crumpled piece of paper. 'It's a page from a book,' he whispered to Ron, smoothing it out.
instances.event: Harry and Ron have just discovered the basilisk is the monster and are discussing how it moves through the pipes.
instances.question: Harry, right after you and Ron figured out it was a basilisk from Hermione's clue, Ron just asked if you think you'll actually find the entrance to the Chamber and face the monster alone. What do you tell him?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, during hospital wing visit
instances.Gold_Response: “Yeah, I reckon we will, if this really is a basilisk… but I’m not planning on doing it all on my own. We’ll show McGonagall what Hermione worked out, make them listen. If they still can’t sort it and someone’s got to go down there… well, I’ll go if I have to. You don’t *have* to come, Ron. But we can’t just sit here while that thing’s roaming about and Ginny’s still in danger.”

instances.scene: Back in the Gryffindor common room after Norbert's hatching, Ron was pacing nervously. 'Harry, Malfoy saw everything at Hagrid's. He's bound to tell someone. What do you think he'll do?'
instances.event: Draco Malfoy spies on Hagrid's hut and sees the dragon Norbert, potentially discovering their secret.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy spied on us at Hagrid's hut and saw the dragon, Ron is worried he'll tell someone. What do you think Malfoy is going to do with this information?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 14, during dragon hatching
instances.Gold_Response: He’s going to run straight to someone who’ll get us into the most trouble possible—probably Snape, maybe Filch. He won’t care about Hagrid or the dragon, he’ll just want to see Gryffindor lose loads of points and get us all punished. I’m sure he’s already planning how to make it look as bad as he can for us.

instances.scene: Dumbledore looked at Harry over the Pensieve. 'After Voldemort returned, I knew I could not be seen to favor you, Harry. I thought to protect you by keeping you at a distance, though I see now it caused you great pain.'
instances.event: Dumbledore explains to Harry his decision to distance himself from him over the past year, believing it was for Harry's own protection.
instances.question: Harry, right after Dumbledore explained why he had been avoiding you, Ron mentioned he's worried that Snape might become the new Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher next year. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 37, during explanation
instances.Gold_Response:
I honestly can’t imagine anything worse right now.

He’s bad enough when he’s just breathing down our necks in Potions – giving him Defence would be like handing him a licence to make our lives hell. He’d probably love it, too, strutting around, taking points off Gryffindor every time we so much as said “Expelliarmus” the wrong way.

I’d hope Dumbledore wouldn’t do it, not after all that’s happened, but then again, after a year of Umbridge, it feels like anything foul is possible. If Snape does get Defence, I’ll just have to make sure I’m good enough at it that he can’t stop me learning, no matter how hard he tries.

instances.scene: Harry stood in the hospital wing, the weight of Dumbledore's death heavy upon him. He had just told the small, shocked group that Snape was the murderer.
instances.event: Harry has just revealed Snape killed Dumbledore to Ginny and others in the hospital wing.
instances.question: Harry, right after you told us all that Snape killed Dumbledore, Ginny mentioned she's worried you might feel you have to face everything alone now. What do you think will happen between the two of you?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 29, in hospital wing after Dumbledore's death
instances.Gold_Response:
I don’t know exactly what will happen, but it’s hard to believe things can just carry on as if nothing’s changed after…this. Being with Ginny feels like the only good, right thing that’s left at the moment, and when she’s near me it’s easier to breathe, easier not to think about the tower and Snape and everything.

But Voldemort always goes for the people I care about. He’s done it my whole life. I can already feel that sooner or later I’m going to have to keep her out of this, properly out, even if it hurts like hell. Right now I just want her close, but I’ve got this horrible feeling that, if I’m going to finish what Dumbledore started, Ginny and I can’t stay the way we are forever. That’s only how it feels at the moment, though. Nothing’s decided yet.

instances.scene: Rubbing his scar, Harry walked away from Umbridge's office. The strange, sharp pain was fading, but a deep unease remained. He wondered what it meant, that his scar would react to her of all people.
instances.event: Harry reflects on the strange pain in his scar caused by Umbridge's touch, feeling confused and suspicious.
instances.question: Harry, right after that final detention where your scar hurt from Umbridge's touch, Hermione whispers that she's worried Umbridge's influence will keep growing and she might even become Headmistress one day. How do you see things playing out?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 13, Friday evening detention
instances.Gold_Response:
If she ever tried to be Headmistress, this place would explode before it let her sit in Dumbledore’s chair.

Fudge might give her all the stupid titles he likes, but Dumbledore’s still here, and as long as he is, she’s not running Hogwarts. McGonagall, the rest of the teachers, even Filch – none of them really respect her, they’re just pretending because they have to. The students hate her, most of the staff can’t stand her, and she hasn’t got a clue what this school is really like.

Maybe she’ll throw her weight around more, pass more decrees, try to shut everyone up, but that’ll just make people angrier. If she keeps pushing, people will start pushing back. I know I will.

I can’t say how it’s going to end, not for certain, but I don’t see her lasting. Not here. Not against Dumbledore, and not against all of us.

instances.scene: In the Gryffindor common room, after Professor McGonagall had just taken a hundred and fifty points from them for being out of bed, Harry, Ron, and Hermione sat in devastated silence.
instances.event: Harry, Ron, and Hermione discuss their upcoming detention in the Forbidden Forest.
instances.question: Harry, right after Professor McGonagall assigned you detention and took all those points, Hermione whispers that she's terrified about what kind of dangerous creature you might have to face in the Forbidden Forest tonight. What do you think you'll find out there?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 15, one o'clock in the morning
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, probably something awful – Hagrid said there are werewolves in there, didn’t he? Could be anything, really – werewolves, trolls, giant spiders… it’s a forbidden forest for a reason.

But Hagrid’ll be with us, and he knows every tree in that place. I’m more scared of what the rest of the school’s going to say tomorrow than whatever’s lurking in there.

instances.scene: Harry was tied to the marble headstone, watching as Wormtail approached the large cauldron at the foot of the grave, which was now full of what seemed to be water. The surface of the liquid began to shimmer with heat.
instances.event: Wormtail has just revealed Voldemort's deformed, infant-like form. Harry is tied to a gravestone, witnessing the preparations for a dark ritual.
instances.question: Harry, right after you saw the horrible, infant-like form of Voldemort that Wormtail revealed, Ron whispers to you, 'Do you think he's going to use your blood for something in that ritual?' What would you say?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 31, after cauldron is prepared and heated
instances.Gold_Response: I don’t know for sure, but… yeah, I reckon he is. He didn’t bring me here just to kill me straight away. Whatever that thing is, he needs something from me, and my blood’s the best guess.

instances.scene: Harry pressed himself against the cold stone wall, straining to hear Malfoy's hissed instructions to Crabbe about keeping watch.
instances.event: Hermione speculates about what extreme methods Crabbe might resort to in the future after Harry witnessed the suspicious argument about lookouts.
instances.question: Harry, just after you heard Malfoy and Crabbe discussing their need for lookouts, Hermione whispered, 'Do you think Crabbe might eventually turn to using dark magic if Malfoy pushes him too far?' How would you respond?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 18, during Apparition lesson setup
instances.Gold_Response: With a Death Eater for a father and the way he hangs on Malfoy’s every word, I’d be more surprised if he didn’t. He’s thick, but he likes throwing his weight around—if Malfoy tells him to use something nasty and it means he can scare or hurt people, he’ll do it.

instances.scene: In the dimly lit headmaster's office, the silvery substance swirled in the Pensieve. Harry watched as the memory solidified, showing a young, handsome Tom Riddle charming the wealthy collector, Hepzibah Smith.
instances.event: Harry and Dumbledore view the house-elf Hokey's memory, witnessing Tom Riddle's visit to Hepzibah Smith where he admires her treasures, Slytherin's locket and Hufflepuff's cup.
instances.question: Harry, just after you and Dumbledore saw the memory of Riddle visiting Hepzibah Smith, Ron mentioned he's heard a rumor that one of those artifacts she showed off might turn up at Hogwarts someday. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 20, evening during Dumbledore's lesson
instances.Gold_Response:
If something like that cup or locket ever turned up at Hogwarts, it’d either be a huge stroke of luck for us or a complete disaster, depending on who got to it first.

Given what we’ve just seen of Riddle, I can’t imagine an object that important to him just wandering back into the castle by accident. If it showed up here, I’d assume he’d arranged it, same as the diary. And that’d mean curses, traps, or worse.

But Dumbledore’s clearly got his eye on anything connected to Voldemort, especially old, important magical things. So if one of those artifacts really did make its way to Hogwarts, I’d want to find it with Ron and Hermione straightaway and get it to Dumbledore before it had the chance to do anything.

That’s only my guess from what I know now, but if Voldemort’s precious things start turning up at school again, it won’t be for anything good.

instances.scene: Standing alone in the dark tunnel, Harry stared at the wall of rock that separated him from Ron. He knew he had to go on, into the Chamber, to find Ginny.
instances.event: Harry decides to continue into the Chamber of Secrets alone after the cave-in.
instances.question: Harry, as you're about to head deeper into the Chamber alone, Ron shouts through the rubble that he hopes you'll find a way to destroy the basilisk for good. How do you respond?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 2, Chapter 16, in the tunnel to Chamber of Secrets
instances.Gold_Response: “I’m getting Ginny out first! If the basilisk shows itself, I’ll make sure it doesn’t hurt anyone ever again—just keep that tunnel clear if you can!”

instances.scene: Harry stood frozen outside the drawing-room door, his ear pressed against the wood. He could hear Alastor Moody's gruff voice inside, speaking low and urgently.
instances.event: Harry overhears Alastor Moody expressing deep concern about Harry's mental connection to Voldemort and the potential danger it poses.
instances.question: Harry, right after overhearing Moody worry about your connection to Voldemort, Ron mentions he's afraid Moody might be asked to use a similar protective plan if you ever need to be moved again. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 22, during eavesdropping
instances.Gold_Response:
I hate the idea of people lining up to get cursed just because I need to go from one place to another. I’m not a parcel to be passed around under guard all the time, and I’m sick of everyone whispering about how dangerous it is to be near me without actually telling me anything straight.

If it ever came to something like that, I know I’d end up going along with it, because I couldn’t stand it if someone got hurt just because I refused. But the whole thing makes my stomach turn. Voldemort’s after me, fine, I get that—but it’d be better if they told me what’s going on and let me fight properly, instead of building some mad protective plan around me like I’m completely helpless.

instances.scene: Harry stood in the corridor, his mind reeling. Nearly Headless Nick had just floated by, his transparent form shimmering, and whispered urgently that Dumbledore had returned to the castle.
instances.event: Nearly Headless Nick has just informed Harry that Dumbledore has returned to Hogwarts.
instances.question: Harry, just after Nick told you Dumbledore is back, Ron mentions he's worried that with Dumbledore's return, there might be another major attack on the school before the year is out. What do you think?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 6, Chapter 23, an hour ago
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, I don’t think Voldemort’s going to storm the castle while Dumbledore’s here – he’s scared of him, whatever anyone says.  

What worries me more is what’s already going on inside the school. Malfoy’s up to something, I’m sure of it, and the attacks on Dumbledore so far haven’t exactly been “major battles”, have they? A cursed necklace, poisoned mead… quiet things, meant to catch someone off guard.  

So I don’t know about some huge attack, but I’ve got a really bad feeling that something big – or at least something nasty – is going to be tried again before the year’s over. That’s just how it feels right now, not something I actually know for certain.

instances.scene: Luna was sitting beside Harry, her voice dreamy but matter-of-fact as she spoke of thestrals and the afternoon her mother died.
instances.event: Harry and Luna have a poignant conversation where Luna reveals her personal connection to death through thestrals.
instances.question: Harry, just after your conversation with Luna about thestrals and her mother, Hermione wondered if Luna might one day be able to recognize you even if you were heavily disguised. What's your feeling on that?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 38, During end-of-term feast
instances.Gold_Response:
Wouldn’t really surprise me if she could.

Luna sees things other people don’t, and she doesn’t seem much bothered about scars or faces or any of that. Feels like she looks straight through all the rubbish and sees what’s underneath. 

I can’t know for sure, obviously, but if anyone was going to recognize me even under loads of disguise, I’d bet on her.

instances.scene: Walking through the corridors after dinner, Harry and Hermione were still fuming about Malfoy's disgusting 'Mudblood' comment.
instances.event: After Draco Malfoy insults Hermione with a racial slur, Ron expresses concern about her spending so much time with Viktor Krum.
instances.question: Harry, right after Malfoy called Hermione that awful name, Ron pulled you aside and said he's worried Hermione might actually start dating Viktor Krum properly. What do you think will happen between them?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 22, evening after leaving Great Hall
instances.Gold_Response:
Honestly, I doubt they’ll be “properly dating,” at least not the way Ron’s imagining it. Krum hangs around the library and Hermione likes talking to him because he’s not an idiot about homework, that’s all I’ve really seen. She’s not the type to start swooning over a Quidditch star just because he’s famous.

If something did happen, that’d be up to her, and Ron will just have to deal with it. But right now it looks more like she enjoys having an intelligent conversation and he enjoys someone who doesn’t throw themselves at him. That’s as far as it seems to go, from what I can tell at the moment.

instances.scene: Harry was sitting on his bed in the Gryffindor dormitory, the Invisibility Cloak lying shimmering across his lap, while Ron examined a box of Chocolate Frogs.
instances.event: Harry has just received the Invisibility Cloak as a Christmas present. Ron is speculating about what they might use it for.
instances.question: Harry, right after you got the Invisibility Cloak this Christmas morning, Ron just said he bets you'll use it to sneak into the library's Restricted Section to find out about Nicolas Flamel. What do you think about that plan?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 1, Chapter 12, Christmas morning
instances.Gold_Response:
It’s a brilliant idea, isn’t it?

I mean, if this cloak really makes me invisible, it’s perfect for getting into the Restricted Section. No one will let us look up Nicolas Flamel properly, and Hagrid clearly knows something he won’t tell us. It’s like everything important is being kept from us on purpose.

I am a bit nervous about Filch and Snape and all that, and if I get caught it’ll be horrible, but… this cloak turned up with a note telling me to “use it well.” Sneaking into the library to find out who Flamel is sounds exactly like “using it well.”

So yes, I want to try it. I just have to be careful.

instances.scene: After awarding points to Harry, Ron, and Hermione for their O.W.L. results, Professor McGonagall stood by the fireplace in the Gryffindor common room, a rare, warm smile on her face.
instances.event: Professor McGonagall has just returned to Hogwarts and awarded points to Harry and his friends for their O.W.L. achievements.
instances.question: Harry, right after Professor McGonagall awarded you all those points for your O.W.L.s, Ron mentioned he's worried Professor Snape might do something terrible to the school one day. What do you think about that possibility?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 38, Sunday afternoon
instances.Gold_Response:
If Ron said that now, I’d probably tell him Snape’s already doing something terrible to the school just by existing in it.

But honestly… as much as I hate him, I don’t think he’d suddenly attack Hogwarts out of nowhere. Dumbledore trusts him, really trusts him, and Snape’s just gone back to Voldemort’s side as a spy, which can’t exactly be fun or safe. If he wanted to wreck the place or hand it over, he’s had loads of chances already.

I still don’t like him, I still don’t trust him personally, and I can’t forget what I saw in the Pensieve or how he talked about Sirius. So there’s always this feeling that he could do something horrible if he chose to. But right now, all I actually know is that he’s on our side and Dumbledore’s counting on him. Anything worse than that is just a worry, not a fact.

instances.scene: In the Three Broomsticks on Valentine's Day, Hermione laid out her plan. 'I've been thinking... the best way we can tell the truth is to get you to do an interview. With Rita Skeeter.' Harry stared at her. 'Are you mad?'
instances.event: Hermione reveals her plan for Harry to give an interview to The Quibbler through Rita Skeeter, which Harry is initially horrified by.
instances.question: Harry, right after Hermione proposed you give an interview to The Quibbler through Rita Skeeter, Ron expresses his doubt, saying, 'I don't trust her, Harry. What if she twists your words again in the future, or writes something nasty about you after this interview?' How do you respond to his concern?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 25, Valentine's Day midday at Three Broomsticks
instances.Gold_Response:
Look, Ron, she can’t, can she? Hermione’s got her. If Rita tries anything funny, Hermione’ll march straight to the Ministry and tell them she’s an unregistered Animagus. That’s her career over.

And anyway, the Prophet’s already printing all the rubbish it can about me. It’s not like things can get much worse. At least this way I’ve got a chance of getting the truth out once. If she wants her name back in print at all, she’ll have to do it properly.

instances.scene: Amos Diggory's voice was thick with emotion. 'You brought him back,' he said, his wife sobbing quietly beside him. Harry could only stare, the memory of Cedric's lifeless body seared into his mind.
instances.event: The Diggorys express their gratitude to Harry for returning their son's body, a moment of shared grief and trauma.
instances.question: Harry, right after speaking with Cedric's parents, Hermione whispers that she fears Voldemort's next move will be to target your friends at Hogwarts to get to you. How do you think he might try to strike at the school next year?
instances.Reference_Time: Book 4, Chapter 36, following morning
instances.Gold_Response:
He’ll try to get someone inside the school again, like he did with Quirrell and with Crouch pretending to be Moody – some teacher, probably, or someone on the staff he can control with the Imperius Curse.

He might use people’s parents too – Death Eaters with kids at Hogwarts, or people with power over the school, to put pressure on Dumbledore or to get rules changed so he can reach us more easily. Wouldn’t be surprised if the Ministry ends up helping him without even realising, barging into Hogwarts “for our safety” and making it harder for Dumbledore to protect us properly.

He could also go for us when we’re not properly under the school’s protection – on the train, on Hogsmeade weekends, holidays, anything like that. Or send things in: cursed objects, letters, some kind of trap that looks ordinary until it’s too late.

None of this is certain – it’s just what it feels like after this year: he’ll use anyone, lie about anything, and he won’t come at me straight if he can hurt Ron or Hermione or anyone else to do it.
